definition_zh: 翻译；译成；转化；解释；被译成
definition_en: to express words in another language, or to change something into a different form or result
core_image: 一句话从一个人嘴里出来，落到另一个人嘴里时换了一副字
scene: 餐桌上，一位老奶奶只会方言，孙女把她的吩咐一句句换成普通话讲给客人听。 She translated her grandmother’s story for the guests.
sceneCN: 这里 translate 是「把话译成另一种语言」（第 1 个义项：口头或书面翻译）；句意为她把奶奶讲的故事译给客人听。话从一张嘴搬到另一张嘴的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ion 构成名词，义为「翻译；译文」
动词加 -or 构成，义为「译者；翻译员」
动词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「可译的」

senses.title: To express in another language
senses.definition: to say or write words again in a different language
senses.definitionCN: 用另一种语言把话语或文字重新表达
senses.example: She translates poetry from Japanese into English.
senses.exampleCN: 她把日本诗歌译成英文。
senses.why: The Latin latus means carried, so to translate is to carry a meaning across into another tongue.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 latus 意为「被搬运」，所以 translate 就是把意义搬到另一种语言里。

senses.title: To turn into another form or result
senses.definition: to change something into a different form or practical result
senses.definitionCN: 把某物变成另一种形式或实际结果
senses.example: Good plans rarely translate into good results easily.
senses.exampleCN: 好计划很少能轻易变成好结果。
senses.why: Once meaning can be carried across, any conversion from one state to another fits the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 既然意义能被搬过去，那么任何从一种状态到另一种的转换都能用这个动词。

senses.title: To explain or understand in one’s own terms
senses.definition: to explain or understand something in a way one can grasp
senses.definitionCN: 用自己能把握的方式解释或理解某物
senses.example: He translated her silence as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
senses.why: Readers carry a text into their own frame, and that carrying is also a translation.
senses.whyCN: 读者把文本搬进自己的框架，这一次搬运同样是翻译。

senses.title: To be capable of being translated
senses.definition: to be able to be put into another language with its meaning kept
senses.definitionCN: 能被译成另一种语言而意义不失
senses.example: This joke does not translate well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个笑话一译就走味。
senses.why: When the load cannot be carried without damage, we say the thing does not translate.
senses.whyCN: 当那担货搬过去必然受损时，我们就说这个东西译不好。

senses.title: To move a bishop to another see
senses.definition: to move a bishop from one diocese to another
senses.definitionCN: 把主教从一个教区调到另一个
senses.example: He was translated to a northern diocese.
senses.exampleCN: 他被调任到北方一个教区。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: a holy man is carried to a new seat.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项：把神职人员搬到新的座位。

intro.en: The verb comes from Latin translatus, the past participle of transferre, to carry across.
intro.cn: 这个动词来自拉丁语 translatus，是 transferre（搬运过去）的过去分词。

items.en: Ferre means to carry, and its participle latus means carried, born, or brought.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 意为搬运，其分词 latus 意为被搬、被承载。

items.en: Translatus is a carrying across, used of moving goods, of people, and later of meaning.
items.cn: translatus 是一次搬运过去，先用于货物与人，后用于意义。

items.en: Old French translater gives English the verb with the sense of turning text into another tongue.
items.cn: 古法语 translater 把这个动词传入英语，含「把文本换成另一种语言」之义。

items.en: English uses it from the fourteenth century for rendering texts, and later for other conversions.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪用它指译文本，后来又扩及其他转换。

items.en: Biology and business extend it to protein synthesis and to results.
items.cn: 生物学与商业又把它扩展到蛋白质合成与成效。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -lat- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other verbs about rendering and explaining.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -lat- 词干，近义组汇集表示转换与解释的其他动词。

entries.definition: the act or result of rendering into another language
entries.definitionCN: 翻译；译文

entries.definition: a person who translates
entries.definitionCN: 译者

entries.definition: to move something to another place
entries.definitionCN: 转移；调动

entries.definition: to connect one thing with another
entries.definitionCN: 使有关联

entries.definition: to express something in another form
entries.definitionCN: 表达；译出

entries.definition: to explain the meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 解释；口译

entries.definition: to restate in other words
entries.definitionCN: 改述

entries.definition: to change into another form
entries.definitionCN: 转换；改变

normalIntro.en: The -lat- inside the word is the Latin participle carried, and it ties the whole family together.
normalIntro.cn: 词中的 -lat- 就是拉丁语分词「被搬运」，把整个词族连在一起。

normal.en: Trans- is across and latus is carried, so translate is to carry meaning across.
normal.cn: trans- 是跨过，latus 是被搬运，所以 translate 就是把意义搬过去。

normal.en: Translation is the act or the text, translator is the person.
normal.cn: translation 是行为或文本，translator 是人。

normal.en: Transfer and relate are cousins, built on the same carried root.
normal.cn: transfer 与 relate 是表亲，建在同一个「搬运」词根上。

normal.en: Ideas can be translated into action, which is the figurative use.
normal.cn: 想法可以 translate into action，这是比喻用法。

normal.en: A joke that does not translate loses its point on the way across.
normal.cn: 译不通的笑话在搬运途中丢了意思。

abstract.en: Picture one sentence stepping off a boat on the other shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话在彼岸下船。

abstract.en: Hear it land in another alphabet, the meaning still whole.
abstract.cn: 听它落在另一套字母里，意思仍然完整。

abstract.en: Then picture the same sentence as a plan, landing as a deed.
abstract.cn: 再把这同一句话想成计划，落地时成了行动。

examples.en: He translates French novels for a living.
examples.cn: 他靠翻译法国小说为生。

examples.en: Their enthusiasm did not translate into votes.
examples.cn: 他们的热情并没有变成选票。

examples.en: I translated his silence as a refusal.
examples.cn: 我把他的沉默理解为拒绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯雷特」——把话穿过一条街，送到雷特先生的耳朵里。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（穿过）+ latus（ferre「搬运」的过去分词），动词 transferre 经古法语 translater 进入英语；同族有 transfer、relate

sensesIntro.en: The senses all describe carrying something across a gap: a language, a state, or a silence.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都描述把某物跨过一道距离搬过去：跨语言、跨状态，或跨过一段沉默。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence leaving one mouth and landing in another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话从一张嘴出来，落进另一张嘴。

branches.en: The language pair: rendering a text, and failing to render it well.
branches.cn: 语言一对：把文本译出，或译不好。

branches.en: The conversion sense, where a plan becomes a result.
branches.cn: 转化义：计划变成结果。

branches.en: The reading sense, where a silence is carried into meaning.
branches.cn: 阅读义：沉默被搬成意义。

branches.en: The church sense, where a bishop is carried to a new seat.
branches.cn: 教会义：主教被搬到新的座位。

branches.en: The plain translating sense, where words are the load.
branches.cn: 朴素翻译义：那担货是词语。

intro.en: The verb is a Latin prefix of crossing plus the participle of the verb to carry.
intro.cn: 这个动词是表示跨越的拉丁前缀加上「搬运」动词的分词。

latinIntro.en: Ferre and its participle latus lie behind a very large English family.
latinIntro.cn: ferre 及其分词 latus 支撑着一个非常庞大的英语词族。

items.example: Transit goods pass through a country.
items.exampleCN: transit 的货物过境一个国家。
latus 支撑着 translate 与 relate。

items.example: Transfer the file to a disk.
Relate the result to the cause.
items.exampleCN: 把结果与原因联系起来。

items.example: The footnote refers to page ten.

definition_zh: 安全的；未受伤害的；稳妥的；保险箱
definition_en: free from danger; not harmed; likely to be right; a strong box for valuables
core_image: 一扇锁好的金属保险箱和一把钥匙
scene: 她把文件锁进了保险箱。 She locked the documents in the safe.
sceneCN: 这里 safe 是「保险箱」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她把文件锁进了保险箱。

pos.zh: 未受伤害的；安然无恙的

derivatives.zh: 安全地；稳妥地
安全；安全性
安全性
保护；保障措施

senses.title: Free from danger
senses.definition: not likely to be harmed or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 不太可能受到伤害或损坏的
senses.example: Keep the medicine in a safe place.
senses.exampleCN: 把药放在安全的地方。
senses.why: The core sense is protection from danger.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是免于危险。

senses.title: Not harmed
senses.titleCN: 未受伤害的；安然无恙的
senses.definition: unharmed after a danger or accident
senses.definitionCN: 经历危险或事故后没有受伤的
senses.example: The children were found safe after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，孩子们被找到时安然无恙。
senses.why: Protection produces the result of being unharmed.
senses.whyCN: 保护带来未受伤害的结果。

senses.title: Reliable
senses.definition: likely to be correct or to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 很可能正确或成功的
senses.example: It is a safe bet that prices will rise.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上涨是很有把握的。
senses.why: Physical security becomes confidence in a choice.
senses.whyCN: 身体的安全转为对选择的信心。

senses.title: Strong box
senses.definition: a strong metal box for keeping valuables
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放贵重物品的坚固金属箱
senses.example: The hotel offers a safe in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店的每个房间都配有保险箱。
senses.why: Protection becomes a container for valuables.
senses.whyCN: 保护变成存放贵重物品的容器。

intro.en: Safe comes from Latin salvus, meaning uninjured or healthy, through Old French sauf.
intro.cn: safe 经由古法语 sauf 来自拉丁语 salvus，意为「未受伤的、健康的」。

items.en: Salvus means uninjured and healthy.
items.cn: salvus 意为未受伤的、健康的。

items.en: Salus means health and safety.
items.cn: salus 意为健康与安全。

items.en: Sauf carries the sense of being unharmed.
items.cn: sauf 保留「未受伤害」的含义。

items.en: Safe means secure from harm.
items.cn: 中古英语中 safe 意为免受伤害。

items.en: Safe also names a strong box.
items.cn: 现代英语中 safe 也指保险箱。

note.en: Safe means protected; save means to rescue.
note.cn: safe 是安全的，save 则是拯救。

entries.definition: to rescue or keep something
entries.definitionCN: 拯救；保存

entries.definition: a wise old person
entries.definitionCN: 智者

entries.definition: the act of selling something
entries.definitionCN: 出售

entries.definition: protected from danger
entries.definitionCN: 安全的；牢固的

entries.definition: not injured or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 未受伤的

entries.definition: able to be trusted
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的

normalIntro.en: Safe covers freedom from danger, the result of being unharmed, and a strong box.
normalIntro.cn: safe 涵盖免于危险、未受伤害的结果，以及保险箱。

normal.en: Keep your passport in a safe place.
normal.cn: 把护照放在安全的地方。

normal.en: The missing climbers were found safe.
normal.cn: 失踪的登山者被找到时安然无恙。

normal.en: It is safer to travel by day.
normal.cn: 白天出行更安全。

normal.en: The shop keeps its cash in a safe.
normal.cn: 这家店把现金放在保险箱里。

normal.en: We wish you a safe journey home.
normal.cn: 祝你回家一路平安。

abstract.en: Picture a locked metal box with a heavy door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁好的金属箱，箱门厚重。

abstract.en: Imagine a child returning unharmed from a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子经历暴风雨后安然归来。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that holds firm under weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一座在重压下依然稳固的桥。

examples.en: The old documents are kept in a safe.
examples.cn: 旧文件保存在保险箱里。

examples.en: Make sure the children are safe.
examples.cn: 确保孩子们安全。

examples.en: It is a safe choice for a first job.
examples.cn: 对第一份工作来说，这是个稳妥的选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: safe 与 save 只差一个字母：先 save（拯救），才有 safe（安全）。

root: 源自拉丁语 salvus（未受伤的、健康的），经古法语 sauf 进入英语，核心义「免受伤害、处于安全之中」。

sensesIntro.en: Safe means free from danger, unharmed, reliable, or a strong box.
sensesIntro.cn: safe 意为没有危险的、未受伤害的、稳妥可靠的，或保险箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked strong box and a key.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁好的坚固箱子与一把钥匙。

branches.en: The base sense is freedom from danger.
branches.cn: 基础义是免于危险。

branches.en: Protection yields the result of being unharmed.
branches.cn: 保护带来未受伤害的结果。

branches.en: Security becomes confidence in a choice.
branches.cn: 安全转为对选择的信心。

branches.en: Protection becomes a metal container.
branches.cn: 保护变成一只金属容器。

branches.en: Danger avoided and harm escaped overlap.
branches.cn: 避开危险与逃过伤害相互重叠。

intro.en: Safe comes from Latin salvus and builds a family with safety, safely, and safeguard.
intro.cn: safe 来自拉丁语 salvus，并构成 safety、safely 与 safeguard 等词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin salvus and salus are the distant sources of safe and safety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salvus 与 salus 是 safe 与 safety 的远源。

items.example: The money is in the safe.
They tested the safeness of the water.
items.exampleCN: 他们检测了水的安全性。

items.example: This route is safer at night.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线在夜里更安全。

items.example: It is the safest place to wait.
items.exampleCN: 这是最安全的等候地点。

items.example: The bridge is unsafe after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水过后这座桥不安全。

items.meaning: a person who opens safes illegally
items.example: The safecracker was caught at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 撬保险箱的盗贼在黎明时被抓。

latinEntries.example: Salvus gives the core sense of safe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salvus 提供 safe 的核心含义。

latinEntries.example: Salus is the source of safety.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salus 是 safety 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Salvare is related to being safe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salvare 与「安全」这一概念相关。

definition_zh: 取来；接来；去拿；卖给；吸引住
definition_en: to go somewhere and bring back someone or something
core_image: 跑一趟再回来：人离开原地，把要的东西带回到出发点
scene: 狗把球甩进了草丛，主人朝它招手。 The dog ran into the grass to fetch the ball.
sceneCN: 这里 fetch 是「取来、衔回」（第 1 个义项：去把东西拿回来）；句意为狗跑进草丛把球衔回来。

pos.zh: 动词：去取来、去接来；衔回
及物动词：卖得（某价钱）；吸引、使着迷

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转化而来，义为「迷人的、动人的」，是语义的偏移美化
与本词同场的近义表达取回动作，属同义联想而非同源派生

senses.title: To go and bring something back
senses.definition: to go to a place, get something, and carry it back to where you started
senses.definitionCN: 去某个地方拿到东西，再带回出发的地方
senses.example: Please fetch my glasses from the bedroom.
senses.exampleCN: 请到卧室把我的眼镜拿来。
senses.why: The core image is a round trip: leave, get, return with the thing in hand.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是跑一个来回：离开、拿到、带着东西返回原地。

senses.title: To go and bring a person back
senses.definition: to go to where someone is and bring them back with you
senses.definitionCN: 到某人所在之处把人接回来
senses.example: I will fetch the kids from school at four.
senses.exampleCN: 我四点去学校接孩子们。
senses.why: The same round trip applies to people instead of objects.
senses.whyCN: 同样的来回行程，只是对象从物换成了人。

senses.title: To sell for a price
senses.definition: to be sold for a particular amount of money
senses.definitionCN: 以某个价钱卖出
senses.example: The old painting fetched over a million yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅旧画卖了一百多万元。
senses.why: The thing travels away from you like a returned object, and money comes back in its place.
senses.whyCN: 物品像被衔回的东西一样离开你，回来的是钱，由此长出售价义。

senses.title: To interest or attract someone
senses.definition: to be interesting or attractive enough to hold someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 足够有趣或动人，能抓住某人的注意力
senses.example: That strange story really fetched the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 那个奇怪的故事把全班都吸引住了。
senses.why: What is brought back from a trip is attention itself, so the mind is carried away and returned.
senses.whyCN: 被带回来的其实是注意力，心被带走又被送回，于是有了吸引义。

intro.en: Fetch goes straight back to Old English, where the same verb meant to pursue and obtain.
intro.cn: fetch 直接来自古英语，同一个动词当时就表示追赶并拿到。

items.en: A Germanic verb family about pursuing and getting underlies the word.
items.cn: underlying 是一个关于追赶和获取的日耳曼语动词家族。

items.en: Old English feccan meant to fetch, to seek and bring back.
items.cn: 古英语 feccan 表示去取、寻找并带回。

items.en: The spelling settled as fecchen, keeping the bring-back meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写定为 fecchen，保留带回的含义。

items.en: The price sense appeared later, then the informal attract sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中先出现售价义，后又产生口语化的吸引义。

items.en: The modern language keeps the word in daily use.
items.cn: 现代英语仍在日常使用该词。

note.en: Fetch, bring, take and get are easy to mix because they all move things around.
note.cn: fetch、bring、take、get 都在搬东西，容易混用。

entries.definition: the past tense of fetch
entries.definitionCN: fetch 的过去式，表示已经取来

entries.definition: to cut a design into a surface with acid; only spelled similarly
entries.definitionCN: 用酸在表面刻出图案；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a quick rough drawing; only looks similar at the end
entries.definitionCN: 速写、草图；只是结尾拼写相近，并非同源

entries.definition: to carry something toward the speaker
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带向说话者一方，强调方向

entries.definition: to carry something away from the speaker
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从说话者一方带走，方向相反

entries.definition: to obtain or receive something in any way
entries.definitionCN: 以任何方式获得或拿到，比 fetch 更笼统

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to keep fetch on the tip of your tongue.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子，让 fetch 随叫随到。

normal.en: Fetch sounds like a short dash: a quick trip out and back with the thing in hand.
normal.cn: fetch 听起来像一次短促冲刺：跑出去、带回来。

normal.en: A dog owner says fetch, and the dog does the round trip.
normal.cn: 主人喊 fetch，狗就完成一趟来回。

normal.en: Think of fetch water: you leave the tap empty-handed and return with a full bucket.
normal.cn: 想 fetch water：空手去水龙头，提着满桶回来。

normal.en: In markets, the goods fetch money, the round trip ends with cash instead of goods.
normal.cn: 在市场里，货物 fetch 出价钱，往返的结果是换回现金。

normal.en: Fetch and carry describes someone always running small errands.
normal.cn: fetch and carry 形容总在跑腿打杂的人。

abstract.en: Every fetch has two ends: where you leave and where you return.
abstract.cn: 每次 fetch 都有两个端点：出发地与返回地。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow that goes out and curls back like a boomerang.
abstract.cn: 想象一支飞出去又回旋的箭，去而复返。

abstract.en: The word itself travels: it leaves your mouth and brings the action back to your feet.
abstract.cn: 这个词自己也在旅行：从嘴里出发，把动作带回脚边。

examples.en: Could you fetch me a glass of water?
examples.cn: 你能给我取一杯水来吗？

examples.en: The house fetched a high price at the auction.
examples.cn: 那栋房子在拍卖会上卖出了高价。

definition_zh: 没有一个；一点也没有；没有人；没有一件东西
definition_en: not one and not any; no person and no thing at all; also used in fixed phrases meaning nobody except
core_image: 一只空碗倒扣在桌上，碗底一粒米也没有
scene: 雨后的院子里，桌上那只碗倒扣着，碗底干干净净。 None of the seats in the hall had been reserved.
sceneCN: 这里 none 是「没有一个」（第 1 个义项：数量上一点也没有）；句意是大厅里的座位一个也没有被预订。图中可辨识物件：倒扣的碗、空桌、雨后的院子。

pos.zh: 没有一个；一点也没有；没有人

derivatives.zh: 由 no 与 thing 复合而成，义为「没有什么」
由 no 与 body 复合而成，义为「没有人」
由 none、the、less 三部分组合而成，义为「尽管如此」
由同一个古英语否定词简化而来，义为「没有」

senses.title: Not any amount or number of something
senses.definition: not any quantity or number of a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 某一事物的任何数量或数目都不存在
senses.example: None of the milk in the fridge was still fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里的牛奶没有一瓶还是新鲜的。
senses.why: The word began as a compressed phrase meaning not one, so its first job is to deny even the smallest unit of whatever is being counted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是「不是一个」的压缩说法，所以它最初的本职就是连所数之物的最小单位也一并否认。

senses.title: Not a single person
senses.definition: no person at all in a group that has just been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚提到的那群人中一个也没有
senses.example: None of the neighbours heard the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居中没有一个人听到警报。
senses.why: Because people can be counted one by one like objects, the same denial of a single unit slides from things to persons without a new word being coined.
senses.whyCN: 因为人可以像东西一样一个个数，同一个「连一个都不」的否认就从物滑到人身上，不必另造新词。

senses.title: No thing of the needed kind
senses.definition: no thing at all of the kind that is wanted or expected
senses.definitionCN: 想要或期待的那类东西一件也不存在
senses.example: I asked for a spare key, but there was none.
senses.exampleCN: 我想找一把备用钥匙，却一把也没有。
senses.why: When the group is left unspoken, the word stands alone, and standing alone it simply reports that nothing of the needed kind is there.
senses.whyCN: 当所指的那一组被省略不说，这个词就独自站住；独自站住时，它只报告需要的那类东西一件也不在。

senses.title: Nobody except; only
senses.definition: used in the phrase none but to mean no person except the one named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 none but 这一说法，表示除所说的那一个之外再无别人
senses.example: None but the captain knew the full route.
senses.exampleCN: 除了船长，没有人知道完整航线。
senses.why: The phrase none but first clears away everyone else and then admits a single exception, so a total denial turns into the narrowest possible only.
senses.whyCN: none but 这个说法先把其余人全部清走，再放进唯一的例外，于是彻底的否认转成了范围最窄的「只有」。

intro.en: None is an Old English fusion of a negative particle and the number one, and its whole history is visible in that join.
intro.cn: none 是古英语里否定小词与数词「一」的融合，它的整段历史都写在这个接合处。

items.en: The negative element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic particle of denial, usually written ne, which also stands behind English no and not.
items.cn: 这个否定成分可上溯到一个通常写作 ne 的日耳曼语重构否定小词，英语的 no 与 not 也由它而来。

items.en: Nān was built from ne, not, and ān, one, and it meant not one, already covering both quantities and persons.
items.cn: nān 由 ne（不）与 ān（一）构成，意为「不是一个」，当时已同时覆盖数量和人。

items.en: Middle English kept the word as noon and none, and the form none won out in the written language.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 noon 与 none 两种形式，最后 none 在书面语中胜出。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the spelling was fixed as none, and the phrase none but was already used for the single exception.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，拼写固定为 none，而 none but 这一说法已用来指唯一的例外。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for quantities, for people and for absent things, while the old link with one survives only in its spelling history.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指数量、指人、也指不在场的东西，而它与 one 的古老联系只留在拼写史里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the negative family built from the same Old English pieces; the near-meaning group collects other words for nothing at all.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批古英语构件搭成的否定词族；近义组收其他表示「一点也没有」的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a fusion of ne, not, and ān, one, so every sense still carries the ghost of a denied unit.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 ne（不）与 ān（一）的融合，所以每个义项里都还带着一个被否认的单位的影子。

normal.en: The word is a fusion of ne, not, and ān, one, so it literally says not one.
normal.cn: 这个词是 ne（不）与 ān（一）的融合，字面上说的就是「不是一个」。

normal.en: The one inside the word is the same word as the number one, which is why the spelling looks like no plus one.
normal.cn: 词里的 ān 就是数词「一」，所以拼写看起来像 no 加 one。

normal.en: None of takes a singular or a plural noun depending on what is being counted.
normal.cn: none of 后面接单数还是复数，取决于所数的是什么。

normal.en: None but and none other than narrow the field down to a single exception.
normal.cn: none but 与 none other than 把范围收窄到唯一的例外。

normal.en: Nobody and nothing were built the same way, by putting a negative before a general noun.
normal.cn: nobody 与 nothing 用的是同一种造法：在泛指名词前放一个否定成分。

abstract.en: A word made by saying not one reminds us that English often builds a total denial out of the smallest possible unit.
abstract.cn: 一个靠说「不是一个」造出来的词提醒人：英语常拿最小的单位来搭出彻底的否认。

abstract.en: Standing alone, the word turns a missing thing into a subject of its own, so absence can be spoken of as if it were present.
abstract.cn: 独自站住时，这个词把缺席的东西变成自己的主语，于是「没有」也能像在场一样被谈论。

abstract.en: Because it denies a count rather than a quality, it fits things, people and empty places without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 因为它否认的是数目而不是性质，所以它不必变形就能套用于物、人和空处。

examples.en: None of the milk in the fridge was still fresh.
examples.cn: 冰箱里的牛奶没有一瓶还是新鲜的。

examples.en: None of the neighbours heard the alarm.
examples.cn: 邻居中没有一个人听到警报。

examples.en: I asked for a spare key, but there was none.
examples.cn: 我想找一把备用钥匙，却一把也没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「难」——一问有没有，回答一声「难」，就是一点也没有；记住 none 是一个也没有。

root: 古英语 nān，由 ne（不）与 ān（一）构成，字面为「不是一个」；中古英语写作 noon 或 none，一般认为十六世纪起固定为 none。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a denied single unit; it divides into a denial of quantity, of persons, of available things and of everyone but one exception.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是被否认的单个单位；由此分出对数量的否认、对人的否认、对现有之物的否认，以及对「除一个例外之外所有人」的否认。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin non and nullus are different formations rather than the source of this pronoun.

definition_zh: 拿着；握住；举行；容纳；持有（观点等）
definition_en: to have something in your hands or keep it there; to organize an event; to contain; to keep an opinion or position
core_image: 一只手稳稳握住东西不松开；有时握住的是话筒、是会场、是一句观点
scene: 运动会上班长手里攥着班旗，一直没松开。 The monitor held the class flag tightly during the sports meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 hold 是「握住、拿着」（第 1 个义项：用手握住东西）；班长用手攥着班旗，一直保持不松开。

pos.zh: 拿着；握住；举行；容纳；持有
握住；抓着（如 catch hold of）

collocations.zh: 持有票（票在手里或名下）

derivatives.zh: hold + -er（做动作的人）→ 持有者（如 ticket holder 持票人）
hold + -ing → 持有；持有的股份

senses.title: To have something in your hands
senses.definition: to have or keep something in your hands or arms
senses.definitionCN: 用双手或手臂拿住、握住某物
senses.example: She held the baby gently in her arms.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻地把婴儿抱在怀里。
senses.why: The core image is a hand that does not let go; everything else grows from this grip.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只不松开的手，其他义项都从「握住」这一动作长出来。

senses.title: To organize an event
senses.definition: to organize an event such as a meeting or a match
senses.definitionCN: 组织召开会议、比赛等活动
senses.example: Our school will hold a sports meeting next Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校下周五将举行运动会。
senses.why: The whole class or school "grasps" one event in a fixed time and place, so the grip is turned into organizing.
senses.whyCN: 整个集体在固定时间地点「攥住」一场活动，握住的动作就转成了「举行」。

senses.title: To contain
senses.definition: if a container or space holds something, it can contain that amount
senses.definitionCN: 指容器或空间能装下一定量的东西
senses.example: This bottle holds one litre of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个瓶子能装一升水。
senses.why: A container keeps what is inside from escaping, just as a hand keeps what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 容器把里面的东西「扣住」不让跑掉，正如手握住东西不松开。

senses.title: To keep an opinion or position
senses.definition: to keep an opinion, belief or position in your mind without changing it
senses.definitionCN: 在心里保持某种观点、看法或状态，不轻易改变
senses.example: Many people still hold this old belief about the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人仍持有关于月亮的这一古老看法。
senses.why: A thought is held in the mind the way an object is held in the hand; both stay firmly in place.
senses.whyCN: 想法被心里「握住」，就像东西被手里握住一样，都稳稳待在原处。

intro.en: Hold comes from Old English healdan, a common Germanic verb meaning to keep or to guard.
intro.cn: hold 来自古英语 healdan，是日耳曼语族的常用动词，意为保管、守持。

items.en: Old English healdan meant to keep, to guard and to hold in the hand.
items.cn: 古英语 healdan 意为保管、守护，也指用手握住。

items.en: The word belongs to the Germanic family; Dutch houden and German halten are close relatives.
items.cn: 该词属日耳曼语族，荷兰语 houden、德语 halten 是它的近亲。

items.en: In Middle English the verb kept the senses of guarding and grasping, and began to mean keeping an opinion.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，该动词保留守护、抓握两义，并开始表示「保持观点」。

items.en: Modern English added everyday uses such as hold a meeting and hold on.
items.cn: 现代英语又发展出举行会议、稍等（hold on）等日常用法。

items.en: The deeper root before Germanic is reconstructed and not fully agreed on.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族之前的更深词根属重构形式，学界尚无定论。

note.en: The first group keeps words built on hold itself; the second group gives close words about keeping things.
note.cn: 第一组是由 hold 本身构成的词；第二组是表示「拿住、保管」的近义词。

entries.definition: the past form of hold
entries.definitionCN: hold 的过去式，义为「握住过」

entries.definition: a person who has or owns something
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，义为「持有者」

entries.definition: the people living together in one house
entries.definitionCN: 由 house 与 hold 合成，义为「家庭；一家人」

entries.definition: to take and keep a very firm hold
entries.definitionCN: 紧握；抓牢，比 hold 用力更大

entries.definition: to take hold of something quickly or firmly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速或牢牢抓住；也指领会

entries.definition: to take something from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 携带；搬运，强调移动而非停留

normalIntro.en: Build the word from real phrases and relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 用真实搭配和同族词记住 hold。

normal.en: hold + on = keep holding, do not let go
normal.cn: hold + on＝继续握住＝坚持住；打电话时引申为「别挂断，稍等」。

normal.en: held is the past of hold: the hand held it yesterday
normal.cn: held 是 hold 的过去式：昨天那只手握过它。

normal.en: A meeting is held like something gripped by a whole group
normal.cn: 会议像被整个集体「攥在手里」一样被举行——hold a meeting。

normal.en: ticket holder = the person who holds the ticket
normal.cn: ticket holder＝握着票的人＝持票人，-er 表示人。

normal.en: Dutch houden and German halten share the same old root
normal.cn: 荷兰语 houden、德语 halten 与 hold 同根，一家人记三个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closed around a small bird: firm but gentle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻拢住一只小鸟：握得稳，又不伤它——hold 的分寸感。

abstract.en: Picture a hall that holds a thousand people without spilling one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大厅「装下」一千个人，一个也不漏——容纳的画面。

abstract.en: Feel your opinion like a stone kept in your pocket.
abstract.cn: 把观点感受成口袋里一直揣着的一块小石头——持有的分量。

examples.en: He held the door open for the old lady.
examples.cn: 他为老奶奶扶住了门。

examples.en: The classroom holds forty students.
examples.cn: 这间教室能容纳四十名学生。

examples.en: Please hold on a moment; I will check it for you.
examples.cn: 请稍等一下，我帮你查一查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「候的」——候着的那只手一直没放下，稳稳握住东西，就是 hold（握住；持有）。

root: hold 来自古英语 healdan（保管、守持），属日耳曼语族本族动词，荷兰语 houden、德语 halten 同源；更早词根属重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From a hand that will not let go grow four uses: gripping, organizing, containing and keeping beliefs.
sensesIntro.cn: hold 的四个义项都从「不松开的手」长出来：握住东西、举办活动、容纳物品、持有想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that will not let go
core.cn: 核心意象：一只不松开的手

branches.en: the hand grips an object
branches.cn: 手握住实物（义项 01）

branches.en: a group grips one event in time
branches.cn: 集体把一场活动「攥」在固定时间里（义项 02）

branches.en: a container keeps things inside
branches.cn: 容器把东西扣在里面（义项 03）

branches.en: the mind holds an idea in place
branches.cn: 心里把想法握在原处（义项 04）

branches.en: holding on means not letting go
branches.cn: 坚持住就是不松手（义项 01 · 04）

intro.en: Hold is a native Germanic verb with a small but useful English family.
intro.cn: hold 是日耳曼本族动词，词族不大但很常用。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin ancestor; Latin tenere is listed for contrast as the Latin verb of holding.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁祖先；拉丁语 tenere（握、持有）列出作对照。

items.example: Hold my hand at the crossing.
She held the rope all night.

items.meaning: the act of holding; property held
items.example: The bank holds a large share holding.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行持有一大笔股份。

items.example: Hold on, the bus is coming.

items.meaning: a family living in one house
items.example: Every household has a TV now.
items.exampleCN: 现在每家都有一台电视。

items.example: Latin tenere builds contain and retain.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 tenere 构成了 contain 与 retain。

definition_zh: 和平；安宁；和睦；和约
definition_en: a state in which there is no war or fighting; also calm and quiet, friendly relations between people, or a treaty that ends a war
core_image: 两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上
scene: 战事停下的那个清晨，街上第一次没有枪声，人们推开窗，听见鸟叫。 After years of fighting, the two sides finally agreed to make peace.
sceneCN: 这里是「和平」（第 1 个义项：没有战争的状态）；句意是打了多年之后，双方终于同意讲和。画面里有安静的街道、推开的窗与窗外的鸟。

collocations.zh: 处于和平状态；内心平静

derivatives.zh: 由 peace 加形容词词尾 -ful 构成，义为「和平的；宁静的」
由 peace 加 -able 构成，义为「爱好和平的；不爱争执的」
由 peace 与 keeping 复合而成，指以武力或派驻人员维持停火的工作
由 peace 与 time 复合而成，指没有战争的时期

senses.title: Freedom from war
senses.definition: a condition in which nations or groups are not fighting each other
senses.definitionCN: 国家或群体之间不再交战的状态
senses.example: The two countries have lived in peace for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家已经和平相处了五十年。
senses.why: Latin pax named a pact that ended a quarrel, so peace begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pax 指结束争执的约定，所以 peace 的起点是一份协议，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Calm and quiet
senses.definition: a state of quiet and calm, free from noise, worry or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 没有噪声、忧虑或打扰的安静平和状态
senses.example: She longed for peace after a day in the noisy market.
senses.exampleCN: 在吵闹的市场待了一天之后，她渴望安宁。
senses.why: The public sense of a stopped war can be felt by one person as a stopped noise, so the word moves inward from the battlefield to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 公共意义上「战争停止」的感受，落实到个人身上就是「噪声停止」，于是这个词从战场转向了内心。

senses.title: Friendly relations between people
senses.definition: a state in which people are not quarrelling and treat each other in a friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 人们不再争吵、彼此以友好方式相处的状态
senses.example: The brothers made peace after a long silence.
senses.exampleCN: 两兄弟在长久互不理睬之后和好了。
senses.why: Scale the same absence of conflict down to a family or a pair of neighbours, and the word still means that nobody is at war.
senses.whyCN: 把同一种「没有冲突」缩小到家庭或两个邻居身上，这个词仍然表示没有人处在交战状态。

senses.title: A treaty that ends a war
senses.definition: an agreement in which two sides formally stop fighting and settle their differences
senses.definitionCN: 双方正式停止交战并解决分歧的协议
senses.example: The peace was signed in a small town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 和约在一座小镇的礼堂里签署。
senses.why: Because pax first meant the agreement itself, the word can name the signed document and not only the state that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pax 最早指协议本身，这个词就能指签署的文件，而不只是协议带来的状态。

intro.en: Peace goes back to a Latin noun for a pact, and it has never lost the idea that peace is something two sides agree to.
intro.cn: peace 可追到拉丁语中表示约定的名词，它始终没有丢掉「和平是双方谈成的事」这一层意思。

items.en: Pax meant a pact or agreement that ended a quarrel, and it also named the state that followed such an agreement.
items.cn: pax 意为结束争执的约定或协议，也指协议达成之后的状态。

items.en: The genitive pacis supplied the stem seen in pacific and pacify, words about making or keeping agreement.
items.cn: 它的属格 pacis 提供了 pacific 与 pacify 所用的词干，这些词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

items.en: Old French pais carried the Latin noun into French with the sense of peace and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 把这一拉丁名词带入法语，义为和平与安宁。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as pees or pes, and it covered both public peace and personal calm.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 pees 或 pes，既指公共的和平，也指个人的平静。

items.en: Modern English settled on the spelling peace and kept the whole range from treaties to a quiet mind.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 peace，并保留了从和约到内心宁静的整套含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin family of pax and one word that only sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects states of calm and of agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 pax 这一拉丁词族，另加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示平静与意见一致的状态。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between two sides, usually to stop conflict or to cooperate.
entries.definitionCN: 双方达成的正式协议，通常用于停止冲突或开展合作。

entries.definition: Peaceful in intention; also the name of the great ocean.
entries.definitionCN: 意图和平的；也用作大洋的名称。

entries.definition: To calm someone who is angry, or to end fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 使发怒的人平静下来，或平息争斗。

entries.definition: The round green seed eaten as a vegetable; it only sounds like peace, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 作蔬菜食用的绿色圆粒；只是读音与 peace 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A state of being free from worry, movement or noise.
entries.definitionCN: 没有忧虑、动静或噪声的状态。

entries.definition: A state in which people agree and work well together.
entries.definitionCN: 人们意见一致、相处融洽的状态。

entries.definition: An agreement to stop fighting for a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在一定时期内停止交战的协议。

entries.definition: Little or no noise; a still and restful condition.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎没有声响；安静而宜人的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a signed agreement and widens until it can describe a single quiet room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一纸签下的协议出发，一步步扩大，直到能描述一间安静的房间。

normal.en: Pax was a pact, so peace in Latin begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
normal.cn: pax 本是一份约定，所以拉丁语里的和平最初是协议，而不是感受。

normal.en: Pacific and pacify share the same stem, which is why all three words are about making or keeping agreement.
normal.cn: pacific 与 pacify 共用同一词干，所以这三个词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

normal.en: English once wrote pees, which is why the modern spelling looks nothing like the Latin pax.
normal.cn: 英语曾把这个词写作 pees，所以今天的拼写与拉丁语 pax 几乎看不出关系。

normal.en: At peace can describe a country and a mind, because the word covers both public and private calm.
normal.cn: at peace 既能说一个国家，也能说一颗心，因为这个词同时覆盖公共与私人的平静。

normal.en: Peace is usually uncountable, but the plural peaces appears when several separate treaties are compared.
normal.cn: peace 通常不可数，但比较几份各自独立的和约时会出现复数 peaces。

abstract.en: Peace is not the absence of anything but the presence of an agreement that both sides intend to keep.
abstract.cn: 和平不是什么东西消失了，而是双方都打算遵守的那份约定还在。

abstract.en: The same word serves a signed treaty and a quiet evening, suggesting that outer order and inner quiet are made of the same material.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既服务于签署的和约，也服务于安静的夜晚，暗示外在秩序与内心安静由同一种材料做成。

abstract.en: A word that began as a handshake now names what whole nations hope for.
abstract.cn: 一个从握手开始的词，如今成了整个国家的愿望。

examples.en: The treaty brought peace to the region after a long war.
examples.cn: 这项条约在长期战事之后为该地区带来了和平。

examples.en: She sat by the window and enjoyed the peace of the early morning.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，享受清晨的安宁。

examples.en: The two neighbours finally made peace after months of silence.
examples.cn: 两位邻居在数月互不理睬之后终于和好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮斯」——把武器收起来，世界就安静了；peace 就是和平。

root: 来自拉丁语 pax（和约、和平），属格 pacis，经古法语 pais 进入英语；同族词有 pact、pacific、pacify。与表示豌豆的 pea 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an agreement that stops a quarrel; the senses run from war between nations, to quiet around a person, to peace between neighbours, and back to the signed treaty itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让争执停下的约定；义项从国家之间的战争，到人身边的安静，到邻里之间的和睦，最后再回到签署的和约本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands that once held weapons opening and resting flat on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上。

branches.en: a morning when the guns finally fall silent
branches.cn: 枪声终于停下的清晨

branches.en: a quiet window opened to birdsong
branches.cn: 推开窗户听见鸟叫的安静时刻

branches.en: two brothers shaking hands after a long silence
branches.cn: 两兄弟在长久沉默后握的手

branches.en: a treaty signed on a plain wooden desk
branches.cn: 在朴素木桌上签署的和约

branches.en: one word holding a nation, a room and a friendship
branches.cn: 一个词同时托住国家、房间与友情

intro.en: A Latin noun of agreement, its oblique stem and a French reshaping hold the word together, with -ful and -able branching off it.
intro.cn: 一个表示约定的拉丁名词、它的斜格词干以及法语的重塑共同支撑这个词，-ful 与 -able 又从它分出新的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the work of keeping a truce

definition_zh: 处理；发牌；交易；协议；许多
definition_en: to give out cards or share things; to handle a problem; an agreement or amount
core_image: 把一叠卡片一张张分到每个人面前
scene: 班级义卖结束后，大家围在课桌前商量捐出去的金额和剩下的物品。 We made a deal to give half of our profits to the library fund.
sceneCN: 这里 deal 是「协议；约定」（第 3 个义项：双方商定的安排）；句意是我们约定把一半利润捐给图书馆基金。

derivatives.zh: 由 deal 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「商人；发牌人」
由 deal 加 -ing 构成，义为「交易；往来」
deal 的复数名词用法，义为「（商业）往来」

senses.title: Give out cards or shares
senses.definition: to hand out cards in a game, or share things among people
senses.definitionCN: 游戏中发牌，或在人们之间分东西
senses.example: Whose turn is it to deal the cards this round?
senses.exampleCN: 这轮该谁发牌？
senses.why: One hand moves around the table giving equal shares, the picture of fair division.
senses.whyCN: 一只手绕桌分发等量的牌，这就是公平分配的画面。

senses.title: Handle or manage
senses.definition: to take action about a problem or task
senses.definitionCN: 对问题或任务采取行动
senses.example: Our monitor deals with lost-and-found items every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班长每周五处理失物招领的事。
senses.why: Sharing out work until it is finished is the same motion as sharing cards.
senses.whyCN: 把任务一份份「分」掉直到做完，与发牌是同一个动作。

senses.title: An agreement between sides
senses.definition: a business arrangement or bargain agreed by two or more sides
senses.definitionCN: 双方或多方商定的商业安排
senses.example: The two clubs struck a deal to share the training field.
senses.exampleCN: 两家俱乐部达成协议共用训练场。
senses.why: When cards are shared fairly, both players accept the result; business copied the game.
senses.whyCN: 牌分得公平双方都认账，商业便照搬了这个游戏的规则。

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a large quantity, used in phrases like a great deal of
senses.definitionCN: 大量，用于 a great deal of 等短语
senses.example: A great deal of practice went into that perfect jump.
senses.exampleCN: 那次完美的跳跃背后是大量的练习。
senses.why: A pile of dealt cards is a big number in the hand, so the heap of cards became a heap of amount.
senses.whyCN: 发到手里的牌是很大一叠，牌堆便变成了「大量」的意象。

intro.en: Deal began as a simple word for sharing things out.
intro.cn: deal 最初只是个表示「分发」的简单词。

items.en: dæl meant a part or share.
items.cn: 古英语 dæl 意为一份、部分。

items.en: The verb dælan meant to divide and distribute.
items.cn: 动词 dælan 意为分开、分配。

items.en: The root is shared with words for part or portion across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 该词根与日耳曼诸语言中表示「部分」的词同源。

items.en: Card games fixed the dealing sense in daily speech.
items.cn: 纸牌游戏把「发牌」义固定在日常生活里。

items.en: Business talk then built deal as agreement, and a great deal as amount.
items.cn: 商业用语又把 deal 变成协议，a great deal 变成大量。

note.en: These words share the share root or describe handling and trading.
note.cn: 这些词与「份额」词根同源，或描述处理与交易。

entries.definition: a trader or the card giver
entries.definitionCN: 商人；发牌人

entries.definition: past form of deal
entries.definitionCN: deal 的过去式

entries.definition: a university official; spelled close to deal
entries.definitionCN: 系主任（拼写近似，词义无关）

entries.definition: unable to hear; one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 聋的（一字母之差，词义无关）

entries.definition: to deal with or manage
entries.definitionCN: 处理；应付

entries.definition: to succeed in doing something difficult
entries.definitionCN: 设法办到；管理

entries.definition: a part given to each person
entries.definitionCN: 份额

entries.definition: a settled arrangement
entries.definitionCN: 协议；同意

entries.definition: a trade agreed at a price
entries.definitionCN: 交易；便宜货

normalIntro.en: Keep the dealt past form and the card picture.
normalIntro.cn: 记住过去式 dealt 和发牌的画面。

normal.en: deal-dealt-dealt: the a becomes e in the past.
normal.cn: deal-dealt-dealt：过去式中 a 变成 e。

normal.en: deal with = handle a problem.
normal.cn: deal with ＝ 处理问题。

normal.en: a great deal of + uncountable noun, like time or work.
normal.cn: a great deal of + 不可数名词，如时间、工作。

normal.en: a big deal means something important; no big deal means not important.
normal.cn: a big deal 是大事；no big deal 是小事一桩。

normal.en: make a deal = agree with someone.
normal.cn: make a deal ＝ 与人达成协议。

abstract.en: Watch the dealer flip cards one by one around the table.
abstract.cn: 看发牌人绕桌一张张翻牌。

abstract.en: Divide a pizza into fair slices and finish them.
abstract.cn: 把披萨切成公平的几块并吃完。

abstract.en: Shake hands when the bargain is fixed.
abstract.cn: 成交时握一握手。

examples.en: Learning to deal with mistakes is part of growing up.
examples.cn: 学会处理错误是成长的一部分。

examples.en: The class monitor dealt out the new textbooks at the start of term.
examples.cn: 开学时班长分发新课本。

examples.en: It took a great deal of practice before the band sounded good.
examples.cn: 乐队练了大量时间后才像样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「递哦」——把牌一张张「递」给你哦，这就是 deal（发牌、分配）

root: 来自古英语 dæl（一份、部分）与动词 dælan（分配），属日耳曼语系表示「部分」的词族；纸牌固定了「发牌」义，商业引申出「协议」，短语引申出「大量」。

sensesIntro.en: One motion of fair sharing grows into handling, trading and amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: 公平分发的一个动作，长出处理、交易和「大量」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cards dealt one by one around the table
core.cn: 核心意象：把一叠卡片一张张分到每个人面前

branches.en: Cards and shared portions
branches.cn: 牌与分到的份额

branches.en: Handling problems and tasks
branches.cn: 处理问题与任务

branches.en: Business agreements
branches.cn: 商业协议

branches.en: Large quantities
branches.cn: 大量

branches.en: Fair shares become signed deals
branches.cn: 公平份额变成签下的协议

intro.en: Deal keeps an old share-root with simple shapes.
intro.cn: deal 保留着古老的「份额」词根，形态简单。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，这个词属于日耳曼语系。

items.meaning: a university official; spelled near deal, unrelated
items.meaningCN: 系主任（拼写近似，词义无关）
items.exampleCN: the dean of studies（教务主任）

definition_zh: 可怕的；骇人的；糟糕的；严重的
definition_en: causing fear or shock; or extremely bad in quality
core_image: 夜里关灯后墙上的影子突然张大嘴
scene: 山路拐弯处，司机看见对面车灯猛地扑来。 The crash was a terrible sight.
sceneCN: 这里 terrible 是「骇人的」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧的）；句意：车祸现场骇人。

derivatives.zh: 非常；可怕地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
使恐惧（同根动词）
恐怖（同根名词）

senses.title: Causing fear or horror
senses.definition: making people very frightened
senses.definitionCN: 使人极度恐惧的
senses.example: The storm made a terrible noise on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨在屋顶上发出骇人的声响。
senses.why: The root terrere means to frighten: this is the fright itself in adjective form.
senses.whyCN: 词根 terrere 意为吓人：此义就是恐惧本身的形容词形态。

senses.title: Very bad in quality
senses.definition: of very poor quality or standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准极差的
senses.example: The food at that hotel is terrible.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆的饭菜糟透了。
senses.why: Shock at badness borrows the fright word: what is awful is treated as what scares.
senses.whyCN: 对「差」的震惊借用了恐惧词：糟到令人「害怕」的程度。

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: extreme in amount or force
senses.definitionCN: 程度或力度极大的
senses.example: The wall felt a terrible pressure in the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水对墙体形成巨大压力。
senses.why: Fear once measured size: the terrible force is one that dwarfs the person facing it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧曾被用来度量大小：可怕之力就是令人自感渺小之力。

senses.title: Feeling unwell or upset
senses.definition: feeling very ill or unhappy, as in feel terrible
senses.definitionCN: 感到极不舒服或难过，用于 feel terrible
senses.example: She felt terrible after the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后她难受极了。
senses.why: The inner state is described with the outer shock word: the body is under attack by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 用外在的震惊词形容内在状态：身体仿佛被情绪袭击。

intro.en: Terrible comes from Latin terribilis, to be feared, built on terrere, to frighten.
intro.cn: terrible 源自拉丁语 terribilis「令人畏惧的」，词基为 terrere「使恐惧」。

items.en: Terrere meant to frighten away or alarm.
items.cn: terrere 意为吓退、惊骇。

items.en: Terribilis described a thing that deserves fear.
items.cn: terribilis 形容值得畏惧之物。

items.en: Old French terrible fixed the spelling and the strong sense.
items.cn: 古法语 terrible 固定了拼写与强义。

items.en: English used terrible of God, war and punishment before everyday badness.
items.cn: 英语先用 terrible 形容神、战争与刑罚，后才用于日常的「差」。

items.en: Everyday use weakened the fear to simple badness or intensity.
items.cn: 日常用法把恐惧弱化为单纯的「差」或程度。

note.en: Terrible is compared with its fear family and with words for very bad things.
note.cn: 把 terrible 与恐惧词族及表示极差的词对比。

entries.definition: the adverb meaning very or frighteningly
entries.definitionCN: 副词：非常；可怕地

entries.definition: once frightening, now excellent
entries.definitionCN: 原为吓人的，今为极好的

entries.definition: intense fear
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖

entries.definition: very bad or unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 极坏的；令人不快的

entries.definition: extremely bad, with dread in the root
entries.definitionCN: 糟糕透顶的（词根含恐惧）

entries.definition: shocking or very bad
entries.definitionCN: 骇人的；极糟的

normalIntro.en: Real links: terrere to frighten, the terror family, and the everyday terrible weather.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：terrere「吓人」、terror 词族、日常的 terrible weather。

normal.en: Terrere means to frighten: terrible things make you gasp.
normal.cn: terrere 意为吓人：terrible 之事令人倒吸冷气。

normal.en: Terrific flipped its fear into praise.
normal.cn: terrific 把恐惧翻转成了称赞。

normal.en: Terrible weather is bad enough to scare a picnic.
normal.cn: terrible weather 糟到能吓跑野餐。

normal.en: Feel terrible: the shock turned inward.
normal.cn: feel terrible：震惊转向了体内。

normal.en: Terror is the noun, terrible the adjective, terribly the degree.
normal.cn: terror 是名词，terrible 是形容词，terribly 是程度。

abstract.en: Badness is measured in gasps.
abstract.cn: 「差」是用倒吸的冷气来计量的。

abstract.en: Some words age from terror into complaint.
abstract.cn: 有些词从恐怖老成了抱怨。

abstract.en: Fear once drew the map of size and strength.
abstract.cn: 恐惧曾描画大小与强弱的地图。

examples.en: The earthquake was terrible in both size and loss.
examples.cn: 这次地震无论规模还是损失都极为可怕。

examples.en: He made a terrible first impression at the interview.
examples.cn: 他在面试上留下了糟糕的第一印象。

examples.en: She felt terrible about forgetting the meeting.
examples.cn: 她为忘了会议而难受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太惹怖」——太惹人怖了 → terrible 可怕的、糟糕的

root: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」→ terribilis「令人畏惧的」→ 古法语 terrible → 英语 terrible；terrify、terror 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From holy fear to everyday complaint: one adjective covers shock, badness and degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对神的敬畏到日常抱怨：一个形容词覆盖震惊、差劲与程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gasp at something too big or too bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对过大或过糟之物的一声惊呼。

branches.en: The fright itself.
branches.cn: 恐惧本身。

branches.en: Badness big enough to scare.
branches.cn: 大到吓人的差劲。

branches.en: Size expressed through fear.
branches.cn: 用恐惧表达的规模。

branches.en: The gasp turned inward.
branches.cn: 惊呼转向内心。

branches.en: The scale slides from horror to complaint.
branches.cn: 尺度从惊骇滑向抱怨。

intro.en: Terrible belongs to the terrere fear family shared with terrify and terror.
intro.cn: terrible 属 terrere「恐惧」词族，与 terrify、terror 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin terrere, to frighten, gave terribilis, terror and the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terrere「使恐惧」产生 terribilis、terror 及英语词族。

definition_zh: 塑料；塑料制的；可塑的；整形的
definition_en: a synthetic material that can be shaped when soft and then hardened; also describing something easily shaped, or surgery that repairs the body
core_image: 一块温热的软料在指间被捏成任意形状，冷却后定型不变
scene: 雨停后的沙滩上散落着瓶盖与碎屑，志愿者提着袋子弯腰一件件捡起。 Volunteers picked every piece of plastic off the beach after the storm.
sceneCN: 这里是「塑料」这个物质本身（第 1 个义项）；句意为暴风雨过后，志愿者把沙滩上的塑料垃圾一件件捡走。图中可辨识物件：袋口、瓶盖、湿沙。

pos.zh: 塑料制的；可塑的；整形的

derivatives.zh: 由 plastic 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可塑性」
由 plastic 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使塑化；增塑」
在 plasticize 之后加 -er 构成，义为「增塑剂」

senses.title: A synthetic mouldable material
senses.definition: a light artificial material made from chemicals, used to make bottles, bags and countless objects
senses.definitionCN: 用化学原料制成的轻质人造材料，用来做瓶子、袋子等大量物品
senses.example: Most of the bottles in the fridge are made of plastic.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里大多数瓶子都是塑料做的。
senses.why: Greek plastikos described anything fit for moulding, so when chemists found a material that could be poured into a shape and set, the old word for mouldable was ready to name it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 plastikos 指「适合被塑造的」，所以当化学家找到一种可以浇进模子再定型的材料时，这个古老的「可塑」之词正好拿来命名它。

senses.title: Made of plastic
senses.definition: made of plastic rather than metal, glass or wood
senses.definitionCN: 用塑料而非金属、玻璃或木头制成的
senses.example: She packed the sandwiches in a plastic box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三明治装在一个塑料盒里。
senses.why: Once the noun named the material, the same form could stand in front of another noun as an adjective, simply marking what the thing is made of.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指认了这种材料，同一个词形就能站到另一个名词前面作形容词，只标示这件东西是用什么做的。

senses.title: Easily shaped or influenced
senses.definition: soft enough to be shaped, or figuratively easy to influence and change
senses.definitionCN: 软到可以被塑造，也可比喻容易受影响、被改变
senses.example: Young minds are plastic and quick to absorb new habits.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的心智可塑性强，能很快吸收新习惯。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the material sense grew out of it. Anything plastic takes an impression from outside and keeps it, which is why the word also describes a mind that can still be moulded.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，物质义正是从它长出来的。凡是可塑的东西都会留下外来的印记并保持住，所以这个词也能形容一颗仍可被塑造的心。

senses.title: Repairing the body by surgery
senses.definition: connected with surgery that repairs or reshapes damaged or unwanted parts of the body
senses.definitionCN: 与修复或重塑身体受损部位、不满意部位的外科手术有关
senses.example: The burn left a scar that plastic surgery could soften.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤留下的疤可以通过整形手术淡化。
senses.why: Doctors who rebuilt damaged faces spoke of plastic surgery because they were literally reshaping tissue, borrowing the moulding image rather than the material one.
senses.whyCN: 重建受损面孔的医生把这类手术叫作整形外科，因为他们确实在重塑组织，用的是「塑造」的意象，而非「塑料」这种材料。

intro.en: Plastic comes from a Greek word for moulding, entered English through Latin and French, and only later became the name of a material.
intro.cn: plastic 出自希腊语中表示「塑造」的词，经拉丁语和法语进入英语，很久以后才成为某种材料的名字。

items.en: The verb plassein meant to mould clay or form a shape with the hands.
items.cn: 动词 plassein 意为捏塑黏土或用双手做出形状。

items.en: The adjective plastikos described what could be moulded, especially the art of the modeller.
items.cn: 形容词 plastikos 形容可以被塑造的东西，尤其指塑形这门手艺。

items.en: Latin took plasticus from Greek as a learned adjective; it is generally treated as a borrowing rather than a native Latin root.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 plasticus 是从希腊语借来的学术形容词，而非拉丁本土词根。

items.en: French plastique carried both the moulding sense and, from the nineteenth century, the sense of a material that can be pressed into shape.
items.cn: 法语 plastique 既保留「塑造」义，也从十九世纪起指可以被压制成型的材料。

items.en: English plastic first meant mouldable, then named the cheap synthetic material of the twentieth century, and widened again to surgery and to flexible minds.
items.cn: 英语 plastic 先指「可塑的」，随后指二十世纪廉价的人造材料，又扩展到整形手术与灵活的心智。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Greek moulding stem and one near-spelling with a different origin; the near-meaning group gathers words for materials and for being shapeable.
note.cn: 形近组收希腊「塑造」词干上的词，以及一个拼写相近但来源不同的词；近义组收表示材料与可塑性的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being easily shaped or changed.
entries.definitionCN: 可塑性；易变性。

entries.definition: A soft coloured modelling clay sold for children.
entries.definitionCN: 一种给儿童玩的彩色软塑泥，商标名。

entries.definition: A paste that hardens on walls; spelled alike but from Greek emplastron, not from plastikos.
entries.definitionCN: 抹墙用的灰泥；只是拼写相近，源自希腊语 emplastron，与 plastikos 不同源。

entries.definition: Looking or feeling cheap and artificial, like plastic.
entries.definitionCN: 外观或手感像廉价塑料的。

entries.definition: Made by chemical processes rather than found in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 经化学过程制成而非天然存在的；合成的。

entries.definition: Able to bend without breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 能弯曲而不折断的；柔韧的。

entries.definition: Easily pressed or hammered into a new shape.
entries.definitionCN: 容易被压打成型；有延展性的。

entries.definition: Created by people rather than occurring naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 由人造出而非自然形成的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a comment on how easily something takes a shape, and that image still sits under the material, the adjective and the surgery.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是在说某物多么容易被塑成形状，而这幅画面至今仍支撑着材料义、形容词义与手术义。

normal.en: Greek plassein means to mould, so plastic is literally the mouldable stuff.
normal.cn: 希腊语 plassein 意为捏塑，所以 plastic 字面就是「能被塑形的东西」。

normal.en: Plasticity keeps the old adjective stem and adds -ity, naming the quality itself.
normal.cn: plasticity 保留旧的形容词词干并加 -ity，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: A plastic bag is named for its material; a plastic smile is named for its fakeness, the same word pointing at two different judgments.
normal.cn: 塑料袋按材料命名，plastic smile 却按虚假命名，同一个词指向两种不同的判断。

normal.en: Plastic surgery reshapes tissue, so the moulding image survives even where no plastic is used.
normal.cn: 整形手术是在重塑组织，所以即便不用塑料，「塑造」的画面仍然在。

normal.en: Plaster looks close but comes from a different Greek word for a salve, so do not read it as a relative.
normal.cn: plaster 看着像，却出自另一个表示药膏的希腊词，不能当成同族词。

abstract.en: A material named after mouldability is a reminder that a word can describe a possibility before it describes a thing.
abstract.cn: 一种以「可塑性」命名的材料提醒人：词可以先描述一种可能性，再描述一件实物。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers a bottle and a smile, which shows how easily English lets a physical quality slide into a moral one.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既形容瓶子又形容笑容，说明英语很轻易就让物理性质滑向道德评价。

abstract.en: If something is plastic, it is not yet finished; the word quietly suggests that being shapeable is also being open.
abstract.cn: 说某物可塑，意味着它尚未定型；这个词悄悄暗示，能被塑造也意味着保持开放。

examples.en: The toy is made of brightly coloured plastic.
examples.cn: 这个玩具是用颜色鲜艳的塑料做的。

examples.en: Scientists are studying the flexibility and plasticity of the young brain.
examples.cn: 科学家正在研究幼年大脑的柔韧性与可塑性。

examples.en: Plastic waste is choking rivers in many countries.
examples.cn: 塑料垃圾正在堵塞许多国家的河流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉斯提克」——听着像把一团软料啪啪拍在桌上，拍成什么形就是什么形。

root: 希腊语 plassein（捏塑）→ plastikos（可塑的）→ 拉丁语 plasticus → 法语 plastique → 英语 plastic；一般认为拉丁形式是借自希腊语的学术词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is mouldability; from it come the material, the adjective of material, the old sense of being shapeable, and the surgical reshaping of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可塑性」；材料义、表材料的形容词义、古老的「可被塑造」义，以及重塑身体的手术义都由它长出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm soft lump pressed into any shape by the fingers, then cooling and holding that shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块温热的软料在指间被捏成任意形状，冷却后定型不变。

branches.en: a bottle of clear synthetic material standing on a shelf
branches.cn: 货架上一只透明合成材料做的瓶子

branches.en: a lunch box that will not break when dropped
branches.cn: 掉在地上也不会碎的饭盒

branches.en: a child's mind taking the print of a new language
branches.cn: 孩子的心智印下一种新语言的样子

branches.en: a surgeon rebuilding a damaged face
branches.cn: 外科医生重建一张受损的脸

branches.en: the same word describing a lump and a mind
branches.cn: 同一个词既描述软料也描述心智

intro.en: A Greek verb of moulding supplies the stem, a Greek adjective ending makes it descriptive, and English suffixes turn it into a quality and a process.
intro.cn: 一个表示捏塑的希腊动词提供词干，一个希腊形容词词尾让它成为描述语，英语后缀再把它变成「性质」与「过程」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 醒来；唤醒；使觉醒；醒来；守灵；航迹
definition_en: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
core_image: 眼睛在暗里突然睁开，窗外刚从黑变蓝
scene: 凌晨四点，窗外一声闷响，他一下子睁开了眼。 She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
sceneCN: 这里 wake 是「醒来」（第 1 个义项：从睡眠中醒过来）；句意为她四点醒来，再也睡不着。暗里突然睁眼的那一刻，就是这个词的形象。

collocations.phrase: wake to the sound of rain

derivatives.zh: wake 加 -en 构成，义为「唤醒；觉醒」
a- 与 wake 同源，义为「醒着的」
wake 加 -ful 构成，义为「睡不着的；警醒的」
复合词，义为「叫醒；叫醒服务」

senses.title: To stop sleeping
senses.definition: to come out of sleep by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 自己从睡眠中醒过来
senses.example: She woke at four and could not fall asleep again.
senses.exampleCN: 她四点醒来，再也睡不着。
senses.why: Old English wacan meant to come out of sleep, and the word has kept that simple picture for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wacan 意为从睡中出来，这个词把这个简单的画面保留了一千年。

senses.title: To make someone stop sleeping
senses.definition: to rouse another person from sleep
senses.definitionCN: 把别人从睡眠中叫起来
senses.example: The noise of the lorry woke the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的声音把整条街的人都吵醒了。
senses.why: English pairs wacan, to wake oneself, with weccan, to wake another; the two verbs merged into one.
senses.whyCN: 英语本有 wacan（自己醒）与 weccan（使别人醒）两个动词，后来合为一个。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become conscious of something that was unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 意识到原先未注意到的事
senses.example: The town woke to the danger only after the river rose.
senses.exampleCN: 直到河水上涨，全镇才意识到危险。
senses.why: Leaving sleep and coming to awareness are the same movement of the mind, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 离开睡眠与明白过来是心智的同一种动向，这个词于是两义兼具。

senses.title: A watch over the dead
senses.definition: a gathering beside a body before burial, or a vigil
senses.definitionCN: 下葬前守在遗体旁的相聚，或守夜
senses.example: Neighbours kept a wake in the old house all night.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们在那座老屋里守了一整夜灵。
senses.why: A wake was originally a night watch, and watching through the night gave the ceremony its name.
senses.whyCN: wake 原本是一次夜间守望，通夜守看的做法把名字给了这场仪式。

senses.title: The track left in water
senses.definition: the trail of disturbed water left behind a moving ship
senses.definitionCN: 船行进后在身后留下的水痕
senses.example: A small boat bobbed in the wake of the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 小船在渡轮的尾波里上下摇晃。
senses.why: The track behind a ship shows where it has passed, and that visible track became the phrase in the wake of.
senses.whyCN: 船后的水痕标出它经过之处，这道看得见的痕迹便成了短语 in the wake of。

senses.title: A yearly village holiday
senses.definition: in the north of England, an annual local holiday once held at a church dedication
senses.definitionCN: 英格兰北部一年一度的村镇节日，原与教堂献堂日相连
senses.example: The whole village closes for the wake in August.
senses.exampleCN: 八月年节时整个村子都歇业。
senses.why: The night watch before a feast grew into the feast itself, so a village holiday still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 节日前的守夜发展成了节日本身，于是村镇假日仍沿用这个名字。

intro.en: Wake is an Old English strong verb, and the noun for a night watch comes from the same root.
intro.cn: wake 是古英语的强变化动词，名词「守夜」同出这一词根。

items.en: Wacan meant to come out of sleep, and weccan meant to rouse another.
items.cn: wacan 意为从睡中出来，weccan 意为叫醒别人。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic tongues all mean to be awake or to watch.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式都表示醒着或守夜。

items.en: In Middle English the two verbs merged, and woke replaced the older past form.
items.cn: 中古英语里两个动词合并，woke 取代了较早的过去式。

items.en: The noun for a night watch over the dead became the funeral wake.
items.cn: 表示夜间守候的名词发展为守灵仪式。

items.en: Sailors used wake for the water track behind a ship, and the phrase in the wake of followed.
items.cn: 水手用 wake 指船后水痕，短语 in the wake of 随之出现。

note.en: The first group holds the words built on the same root, the second the words for sleep and waking nearby.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词根上的词，第二组收周围与睡醒相关的词。

entries.definition: The usual past tense of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词常用过去式。

entries.definition: The past participle, as in has woken.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，如 has woken。

entries.definition: A more formal verb meaning to wake or to be woken.
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的动词，义为唤醒或醒来。

entries.definition: An adjective for not being asleep, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为醒着的，同出此根。

entries.definition: To get out of bed, the step after waking.
entries.definitionCN: 起床，是醒来之后的动作。

entries.definition: To wake someone, often with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 叫醒某人，常需费力。

entries.definition: A literary verb for waking or being woken.
entries.definitionCN: 文学色彩较浓，义为唤醒、醒来。

entries.definition: The state that waking ends.
entries.definitionCN: 醒来所结束的状态。

normalIntro.en: One short strong verb, three irregular forms, and a noun that means two very different things.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短小的强变化动词、三个不规则形式，再加上一个指两种不同事物的名词。

normal.en: Wake, woke, woken: a strong verb that changes its vowel.
normal.cn: wake、woke、woken：改变元音的强变化动词。

normal.en: Waken and awaken are more formal and more often transitive.
normal.cn: waken 与 awaken 更正式，更多用作及物动词。

normal.en: Wake up is the everyday phrase; up adds no new meaning.
normal.cn: wake up 是日常说法，up 不添新义。

normal.en: In the wake of means following after a ship or after an event.
normal.cn: in the wake of 指跟着船或跟着事件而来。

normal.en: A funeral wake is a watch through the night.
normal.cn: 守灵就是在夜里守着。

abstract.en: See eyelids open while the room is still dark.
abstract.cn: 想房间还暗着，眼皮忽然睁开。

abstract.en: Hear a horn outside split the silence of the morning.
abstract.cn: 听外头号声划破清晨的安静。

abstract.en: Picture a white trail widening behind a ferry.
abstract.cn: 想渡轮身后那条渐渐变宽的白痕。

examples.en: I usually wake before the alarm.
examples.cn: 我通常比闹钟先醒。

examples.en: Please wake me at six.
examples.cn: 请六点叫醒我。

examples.en: The storm left broken roofs in its wake.
examples.cn: 风暴过后留下一片破屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克」——维克在凌晨被闹钟叫醒，睁眼第一件事是关它。

root: 古英语 wacan（醒来）与 weccan（唤醒），同出日耳曼语词根；名词 wake（守夜、航迹）同源。

sensesIntro.en: For a thousand years the word has meant leaving sleep, and the night watch of the same root keeps to itself in a dark corner.
sensesIntro.cn: 一千年来这个词都指「离开睡眠」，同根的夜间守望则独自待在另一个昏暗角落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes opening in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗里睁开的眼。

branches.en: The waking branch: waking at four by oneself.
branches.cn: 醒来分支：四点自己醒来。

branches.en: The rousing branch: a lorry waking the street.
branches.cn: 唤醒分支：卡车吵醒整条街。

branches.en: The awareness branch: a town waking to danger.
branches.cn: 觉醒分支：全镇意识到危险。

branches.en: The vigil branch: a wake for the dead, then a village feast.
branches.cn: 守夜分支：守灵，进而成为村镇节庆。

branches.en: The water branch: a boat bobbing behind a ferry.
branches.cn: 水痕分支：渡轮后摇荡的小船。

intro.en: Wake is short; -en, -ful, -ing, -s and the a- and up particles extend it.
intro.cn: wake 很短，靠 -en、-ful、-ing、-s 以及 a-、up 等成分扩展。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and has no Latin source, so this entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root carries the state of waking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「醒」的状态。

items.example: The short form is the base.
It forms in the wake of.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 in the wake of。
sleep 是醒来所结束的事。

definition_zh: 对话；对白；交换意见
definition_en: a talk between two or more people; the words spoken by characters in a story or play
core_image: 两张嘴一来一回的言语抛接
scene: 英语课上，同桌和我分角色朗读课文。 We read the dialogue between the shopkeeper and the customer.
sceneCN: 这里 dialogue 是「对话」（第 1 个义项：两人之间的言语交流）；句意是我们朗读店主与顾客之间的对话。

derivatives.zh: 由 dialogue 词根加 -ic 构成，义为「对话的」
由 mono-（独）加 -logue 构成，义为「独白」
同词源家族词，义为「道歉；辩护」

senses.title: A talk between people
senses.definition: a conversation between two or more people
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多人之间的交谈
senses.example: The teacher encouraged a dialogue between the two classes.
senses.exampleCN: 老师鼓励两个班级之间开展对话。
senses.why: Two voices cross a bridge of words, throwing meaning back and forth.
senses.whyCN: 两个声音用词语搭起桥梁，把意义抛来抛去，这便是对话。

senses.title: Words spoken by characters
senses.definition: the words that characters say in a play, film or story
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或故事中人物说的话
senses.example: The movie's dialogue is quick and funny.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的对白节奏快而有趣。
senses.why: Written talk freezes a real conversation onto the page.
senses.whyCN: 书面的言语把真实的交谈固定在纸面上，于是有了对白义。

senses.title: An exchange of ideas
senses.definition: a serious exchange of ideas between groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 团体或国家之间认真的思想交流
senses.example: Peace starts with honest dialogue, not shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 和平始于坦诚的对话，而非喊叫。
senses.why: Real understanding needs both sides speaking and listening in turn.
senses.whyCN: 真正的理解需要双方轮流说与听，交流义由此生长。

intro.en: Dialogue comes from Greek words for speaking through or across.
intro.cn: dialogue 来自希腊语中表示「穿越着说话」的词。

items.en: Dialogos meant conversation, from dia- (across) plus logos (word, speech).
items.cn: 希腊语 dialogos 意为谈话，由 dia-（穿越）加 logos（词、言语）构成。

items.en: Plato wrote his philosophy as dialogues between teacher and students.
items.cn: 柏拉图以师生对话的形式写哲学，即《对话录》。

items.en: Latin dialogus and French dialogue carried it westward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dialogus 与法语 dialogue 把它传向西方。

items.en: English took dialogue in the fourteenth century for written conversations.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 dialogue，指书面对话。

items.en: It now names talks in plays, films, classrooms and world politics.
items.cn: 如今它指戏剧、电影、课堂乃至国际交往中的对话。

note.en: These words share the speaking root or describe kinds of talk.
note.cn: 这些词与「言语」词根同源，或同样描述说话方式。

entries.definition: American spelling of dialogue
entries.definitionCN: dialogue 的美式拼法

entries.definition: a long speech by one person
entries.definitionCN: 独白（同根，独语）

entries.definition: words of regret, from logos
entries.definitionCN: 道歉（同根）

entries.definition: a listed list of things
entries.definitionCN: 目录（同后缀 -logue）

entries.definition: a regional way of speaking
entries.definitionCN: 方言（同前缀 dia-）

entries.definition: an informal talk
entries.definitionCN: 谈话；交谈

entries.definition: a friendly light talk
entries.definitionCN: 闲聊

entries.definition: a talk about ideas
entries.definitionCN: 讨论

entries.definition: formal talks to reach agreement
entries.definitionCN: 谈判

entries.definition: one person talking to many
entries.definitionCN: 演讲（一人对众人）

normalIntro.en: Use the two-voices image and the -logue family to remember dialogue.
normalIntro.cn: 用「两个声音」的画面和 -logue 词族记住 dialogue。

normal.en: dia- (across) plus logue (word): words going across.
normal.cn: dia-（穿越）加 logue（词）：词语穿越而过。

normal.en: monologue is one voice, dialogue is two.
normal.cn: monologue 是独语，dialogue 是对话。

normal.en: read a dialogue aloud with a partner.
normal.cn: 和同伴朗读 dialogue。

normal.en: movie dialogue is what actors say.
normal.cn: movie dialogue 指演员的对白。

normal.en: the gue ending keeps the French spelling.
normal.cn: 词尾 gue 保留了法语拼法。

abstract.en: Picture a tennis ball of words flying both ways.
abstract.cn: 想象词语的网球双向飞舞。

abstract.en: Hear two characters answering each other in turn.
abstract.cn: 听剧中人物一问一答。

abstract.en: Feel two ideas meeting and growing together.
abstract.cn: 体会两种想法相遇并共同生长。

examples.en: Our textbook has a dialogue about ordering food in a restaurant.
examples.cn: 课本里有一段关于在餐厅点餐的对话。

examples.en: The play needs two students to read the dialogue together.
examples.cn: 这部话剧需要两名学生一起朗读对白。

examples.en: After the quarrel, a quiet dialogue fixed the friendship.
examples.cn: 争吵过后，一次平和的谈话修复了友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呆而乐格」——两人一问一答像对暗号，呆萌又快乐地「对话」

root: 来自希腊语 dialogos（谈话），由 dia-（穿越）加 logos（言语）构成；本义「言语往来」，引申为对白与思想交流。

sensesIntro.en: Dialogue moves words across between people, pages and nations.
sensesIntro.cn: dialogue 让言语在人与人、书页与国家之间往来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words thrown across a bridge
core.cn: 核心意象：词语在桥上双向飞掷

branches.en: Two people taking turns
branches.cn: 两人轮流说话

branches.en: Scripted words on stage
branches.cn: 台上的台词

branches.en: Talks that build trust
branches.cn: 建立信任的会谈

branches.en: Real talk and written talk
branches.cn: 真实交谈与书面交谈

branches.en: Listening is half of dialogue
branches.cn: 倾听是对话的一半

intro.en: Dialogue is built on Greek roots for across and speech.
intro.cn: dialogue 建立在希腊语「穿越」与「言语」词根上。

latinIntro.en: The Greek root log or logue means word and speech.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词根 log/logue 意为词语、言语。

items.exampleCN: a dialogue between friends（朋友间的对话）

definition_zh: 收音机；广播；无线电；用无线电发送
definition_en: a device that receives broadcast sound; the broadcasting of sound by radio waves; the technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves; to send a message by radio
core_image: 一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发亮
scene: 厨房里，老式收音机的指针在刻度上滑动，水壶的蒸汽把窗玻璃蒙上一层白雾。 She turned the radio down when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 radio 是「收音机」（第 1 个义项：接收广播声音的装置）；句意为电话响时她把收音机的声音调小了。画面里可留意：刻度盘上的指针、冒汽的水壶、蒙雾的窗。

pos.zh: 用无线电发送；用无线电联络

derivatives.zh: radio 与 man 复合，指从事无线电通信工作的人
radio 与 controlled 复合，指靠无线电操纵的
radio- 与 isotope 复合，指具有放射性的同位素

senses.title: A receiving device
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that picks up broadcast sound and plays it
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播声音并播放出来的设备
senses.example: She turned on the radio in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她在厨房里打开了收音机。
senses.why: The device is named by shortening the technical word for wireless communication, so the machine carries the name of the method.
senses.whyCN: 这台设备的名字是「无线通信」这一技术词的缩略，因此机器承袭了方法的名字。

senses.title: Broadcasting by radio waves
senses.definition: the activity or service of sending sound to many listeners at once
senses.definitionCN: 把声音同时发送给许多听众的活动或服务
senses.example: The interview will be on the radio tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这段采访今晚会在广播里播出。
senses.why: Once sound could travel without wires, broadcasting became a public service, and English called it simply the radio.
senses.whyCN: 声音既能不用电线传播，广播便成了公共服务，英语就径直称之为 the radio。

senses.title: Wireless communication technology
senses.definition: the technology of sending signals through space by electromagnetic waves
senses.definitionCN: 通过电磁波在空间中发送信号的技术
senses.example: The message was sent by radio from the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是用船上的无线电发出的。
senses.why: This is the broadest sense: the physical method itself, used by ships, aircraft and stations alike.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的一层：指这种物理方法本身，船只、飞机与电台都在使用。

senses.title: To send a message by radio
senses.definition: to communicate with someone by radio, especially in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 用无线电与某人联络，尤指在紧急情况下
senses.example: The pilot radioed for help as the fog closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 雾合拢上来时，飞行员用无线电求救。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the act of sending a message through the same technology.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指通过同一技术发送消息这一动作。

intro.en: Radio is a shortened form of words built on the Latin word for ray; the technology of wireless signalling took the name of the rays it uses.
intro.cn: radio 是建立在拉丁语表示射线的词之上的词语的缩略；无线通信技术采用了它所使用的那种射线的名字。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke or a ray, a straight line sent out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指辐条或射线，即从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays, and the stem radi- entered scientific language as a combining form.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线，词干 radi- 作为构词成分进入科学语言。

items.en: Early wireless signalling was called radiotelegraphy, sending telegraph messages by electromagnetic waves.
items.cn: 早期的无线通信被称为 radiotelegraphy，即用电磁波发送电报。

items.en: English speakers shortened the long technical word to radio in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，英语使用者把这个冗长的技术词缩略为 radio。

items.en: Modern English uses radio for the device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of signalling.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radio 指设备、广播服务、技术以及发送信号的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for broadcasting and wireless signalling.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的词；近义组收表示广播与无线通信的词。

entries.definition: A detection system using reflected radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 利用反射无线电波进行探测的系统。

entries.definition: A line from the centre of a circle to its edge.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条线。

entries.definition: Energy sent out as waves or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式发出的能量。

entries.definition: A person who works with radio equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 从事无线电设备工作的人。

entries.definition: To send sound or pictures to many receivers.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音或图像发送给许多接收者。

entries.definition: Working without connecting wires.
entries.definitionCN: 不通过连接导线工作的。

entries.definition: A device that picks up transmitted signals.
entries.definitionCN: 接收所传送信号的装置。

entries.definition: The sending out of signals or power.
entries.definitionCN: 信号或能量的发送。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin ray in modern dress: wireless signalling was named after the rays that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是穿上现代外衣的拉丁语「射线」：无线通信以承载它的射线命名。

normal.en: Radio, radius and radiation all begin with the Latin word for a ray leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radio、radius 与 radiation 都从拉丁语表示「从中心射出的射线」一词开始。

normal.en: On the radio names the service, while a radio names the box on the kitchen table.
normal.cn: on the radio 指广播服务，而 a radio 指厨房桌上的那台机器。

normal.en: Radio silence means no signals are being sent, often by a ship or an aircraft that must stay unheard.
normal.cn: radio silence 指不发送任何信号，常是船只或飞机必须保持静默时。

normal.en: To radio someone is to send a message by radio rather than by phone.
normal.cn: to radio 某人就是用无线电而不是电话发送消息。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging, a child of the same technology.
normal.cn: radar 是无线电探测与测距，是同一技术的产物。

abstract.en: Radio made a voice present in millions of rooms at once, the first everyday experience of shared listening.
abstract.cn: 广播让一个声音同时出现在千万个房间里，这是人们第一次日常体验到共同收听。

abstract.en: A device named after invisible rays taught people to trust what they could hear but not see.
abstract.cn: 一台以看不见的射线命名的机器，教会人们去相信听得到却看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radio silence is powerful because absence of signal is also a message.
abstract.cn: 无线电静默之所以有力，是因为没有信号本身也是一种消息。

examples.en: The radio on the shelf still works after forty years.
examples.cn: 架子上那台收音机用了四十年还能工作。

examples.en: Her talk will be broadcast on the radio this evening.
examples.cn: 她的谈话今晚将在广播中播出。

examples.en: The coast guard radioed the fishing boat to warn it of the storm.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用无线电通知渔船有暴风雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞迪欧」——声音不用电线，像射线一样飘进屋里，记住 radio 是收音机、无线电。

root: 拉丁语 radius（射线、辐条）→ radiare（发出射线）→ 科学构词成分 radi- → radiotelegraphy → 缩略为英语 radio；同族有 radar、radiation、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is signalling by rays; the senses divide into the receiving device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of sending a message.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠射线传信」；义项分为接收设备、广播服务、技术本身，以及发送消息的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old radio's needle resting on a dial, its speaker faintly warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发热。

branches.en: a dial turned by a thumb
branches.cn: 拇指转动的刻度盘

branches.en: a voice filling a kitchen
branches.cn: 填满厨房的一个声音

branches.en: an aerial on a ship's roof
branches.cn: 船顶的一根天线

branches.en: a message sent through fog
branches.cn: 穿过雾发出去的一条消息

branches.en: the same signal, once as a machine and once as a programme
branches.cn: 同一个信号，一次是机器，一次是节目

intro.en: The word is a modern shortening of a scientific compound built on the Latin stem for ray, with English endings for people and instruments.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「射线」词干上的科学复合词的现代缩略，加上表示人与器械的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radi- is shared with radius and radiation, and it still builds new technical words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radi- 与 radius、radiation 共用，至今仍在构成新的技术词。

definition_zh: 善意；仁慈；亲切的行为
definition_en: the quality of being warm and helpful, and an act that shows it
core_image: 雨里有人把伞悄悄偏过去半个伞面
scene: 车棚下只有一把伞，撑伞的人往旁边挪了挪。 Her small kindness, sharing one umbrella in the rain, made the whole walk bearable.
sceneCN: 这里 kindness 是「善意的举动」（第 2 个义项：体现善意的行为），句意是她雨中同撑一把伞的小小善意让整段路都变得好过了。画面里有车棚、一把伞和被雨打湿的肩头。
