senses.title: The quality of being warm-hearted
senses.definition: the quality of caring about others and wanting to help them
senses.definitionCN: 关心他人并愿意相助的品质
senses.example: Kindness runs in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人代代都心善。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective for a warm nature into the name of that nature itself.
senses.whyCN: -ness 把表示温和天性的形容词变成了这种天性本身的名字。

senses.title: A concrete act that shows it
senses.definition: a specific helpful act, counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 一次一次可数的具体帮助行为
senses.example: She did him a kindness and asked for nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她帮了他一个忙，什么也没要。
senses.why: English lets one suffix name both a quality and its instances, so the noun counts acts as well as moods.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个后缀既指性质又指具体事例，所以这个名词既能量举动也能量心态。

senses.title: Gentle treatment of the vulnerable
senses.definition: the care given to animals, children, or the sick because they cannot repay it
senses.definitionCN: 因为对方无力回报而对动物、孩子或病人给予的照顾
senses.example: He treats old horses with great kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老马十分体贴。
senses.why: Kindness is most visible where it cannot be repaid, so the word is drawn to the weak and the dependent.
senses.whyCN: 善意在无法回报的地方最显眼，所以这个词被引向弱小和依赖者。

senses.title: A softening habit in speech
senses.definition: the habit of saying things so that no one is humiliated
senses.definitionCN: 习惯把话说得不让任何人难堪
senses.example: There was kindness even in his refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 就连他拒绝时也带着体贴。
senses.why: Because kindness is judged by its effect on listeners, a way of phrasing counts as the quality itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为善意要看听者的感受，所以一种措辞方式本身也算作这种品质。

senses.title: Both the giving and the receiving
senses.definition: the relationship opened up when one person helps and another accepts help
senses.definitionCN: 一人给予、另一人接受时所形成的关系
senses.example: Kindness given freely usually comes back.
senses.exampleCN: 白给的善意往往会回来。
senses.why: The word names a bond rather than a single person, because the act needs two sides to exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种关系而非一个人，因为这种行为需要两边才能成立。

intro.en: Kindness is a native English formation: the old word for inborn nature, given the suffix that names a quality.
intro.cn: kindness 是英语本土构成：把表示天生天性的旧词，配上表示性质的后缀。

items.en: The base gecynd meant nature or inborn quality, the same root that gives kin.
items.cn: 词基 gecynd 指天性、天生的品质，与 kin 同根。

items.en: The shortened form kind developed the sense of gentle and well-disposed.
items.cn: 缩简形式 kind 发展出「温和、心地好」的义项。

items.en: The suffix -nes, later -ness, named a quality, so kindnes meant a gentle disposition.
items.cn: 后缀 -nes 后作 -ness，表示性质，于是 kindnes 指温和的性情。

items.en: The countable sense of an act of kindness appears as the word spreads into everyday courtesy talk.
items.cn: 随这个词进入日常礼貌用语，出现了可数的「一件善举」义。

items.en: Kindness of strangers became a fixed phrase in English writing on city life.
items.cn: 「陌生人的善意」在书写城市生活的英语里成为固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -ness and -ly family built on kind; the near-meaning group holds other words for goodwill.
note.cn: 形近组收由 kind 加 -ness、-ly 的词族；近义组收其他表示好意的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun behind this quality word.
entries.definitionCN: 这个品质词所依赖的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, warm in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的副词，指和善地。

entries.definition: A near twin, built from kindly plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kindly 加 -ness 构成的近义双胞胎词。

entries.definition: Family, the oldest sense of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 亲族，是这个词根最古老的含义。

entries.definition: Moral good quality, wider and more general.
entries.definitionCN: 指道德上的善，范围更宽更泛。

entries.definition: A free and giving spirit, often with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指大方慷慨，常与钱财有关。

entries.definition: Deep sympathy for someone who suffers.
entries.definitionCN: 指对受苦者的深切同情。

entries.definition: The deliberate causing of pain, the reverse of kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意施加痛苦，是 kindness 的反面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the -ness suffix to a root about inborn nature, and to the small acts people notice.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -ness 后缀系在表示天性的词根上，也系在人们看得见的小举动上。

normal.en: Kind plus -ness names a quality, not a person.
normal.cn: kind 加 -ness 命名的是性质，不是人。

normal.en: Kindly and kindness split adverb from noun.
normal.cn: kindly 与 kindness 一个是副词一个是名词。

normal.en: Unkindness adds un- for the harsh opposite.
normal.cn: unkindness 加 un- 表示刻薄的反面。

normal.en: An act of kindness counts one helpful deed.
normal.cn: an act of kindness 数的是具体的一件好事。

normal.en: Out of kindness explains the motive, not the action.
normal.cn: out of kindness 说明的是动机而非行动。

abstract.en: Kindness is an umbrella tipped a little toward the other shoulder.
abstract.cn: 善意就是把伞稍稍偏向别人的肩。

abstract.en: A quality word with a countable sense means it can be counted in deeds.
abstract.cn: 一个能计数的性质词，意味着它可以按举动来数。

abstract.en: Kin and kindness come from one root: warmth begins with those nearest.
abstract.cn: kin 与 kindness 同源：温暖从最近的人开始。

examples.en: He never forgot her kindness in that hard year.
examples.cn: 那艰难的一年里她的善意他从未忘记。

examples.en: Small kindnesses make a long journey lighter.
examples.cn: 小小的善举让漫长的旅程轻快些。

examples.en: She thanked the nurse for her kindness.
examples.cn: 她感谢护士的照顾和善意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯得奈斯」——肯得下心把好先给人，就是善意

root: 古英语 gecynd（天性）派生 kind，加名词后缀 -ness（古英语 -nes）构成 kindness，由「天生温和的性情」扩展出「善举」的可数用法；与 kin 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the quality itself, a countable helpful act, care for the weak, a softening way of speech, and the bond between giver and receiver.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：品质本身、可数的善举、对弱者的照顾、说话留余地的习惯，以及施与受之间的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warmth offered from one person's hand to another's.
core.cn: 核心意象：暖意从一个人的手递到另一个人的手上。

branches.en: THE QUALITY LINE: a mood and its countable deeds.
branches.cn: 品质这条线：一种心态和可数的举动。

branches.en: THE WEAK LINE: care where nothing can be repaid.
branches.cn: 弱者这条线：得不到回报处的照顾。

branches.en: THE VOICE LINE: kindness heard in phrasing.
branches.cn: 声音这条线：从措辞里听到的体贴。

branches.en: THE BOND LINE: an act that needs two sides.
branches.cn: 关系这条线：必须有两边才成立的行为。

branches.en: THE LIFE LINE: from inborn nature to a returned favour.
branches.cn: 生活这条线：从天生性情到回报的好意。

definition_zh: 允许；准许；给予；留出
definition_en: to let something happen, or to give time or money for a purpose
core_image: 老师点头让学生提前离开
scene: 教室里，老师点头同意一名学生提前离开。 The teacher allowed him to go home early.
sceneCN: 这里 allowed 是「允许」（第 1 个义项：准许某人做某事）；句意为老师允许他早点回家。

pos.zh: 动词：允许；准许；给予；留出

senses.title: To give permission
senses.definition: to let a person do something
senses.definitionCN: 让某人做某事
senses.example: The teacher allowed him to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 老师允许他离开。
senses.why: The French verb meant to grant, so letting someone do something is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词意为准许，所以让某人做某事就是第一义。

senses.title: To let something happen
senses.definition: to make it possible for an event to take place
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事得以发生
senses.example: The open window allowed fresh air in.
senses.exampleCN: 开着的窗让新鲜空气进来。
senses.why: The same granting was widened from people to events and things.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「准许」从人扩展到事件与事物。

senses.title: To set aside time or money
senses.definition: to plan an amount of time or money for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个用途计划出时间或钱
senses.example: Allow an hour for the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这段路要留出一小时。
senses.why: Granting a share of one's time or money is the planning sense of allowing.
senses.whyCN: 从自己的时间或钱里让出一份，就是安排上的留出。

senses.title: To take into account
senses.definition: to think about something when making a plan
senses.definitionCN: 做计划时把某事考虑进去
senses.example: Allow for the wind on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 要考虑到山上的风。
senses.why: Making room in a plan for a difficulty is the phrase allow for.
senses.whyCN: 在计划里为困难让出空间，就是 allow for。

intro.en: The recorded history of allow is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 allow 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Allaudare meant to praise, and it fed into the French verb.
items.cn: allaudare 意为称赞，它进入了法语动词。

items.en: Allocare meant to place or to assign something to someone.
items.cn: allocare 意为放置或把某物分配给某人。

items.en: Alouer carried both giving and permitting into English.
items.cn: alouer 把给予与准许两层意思带进英语。

items.en: English used allow for granting a request.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 allow 指准许请求。

items.en: Today it also covers time, money and planning for a problem.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖时间、金钱与为问题做打算。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，指津贴或允许量。

entries.definition: A more formal word for giving permission.
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的准许说法。

entries.definition: A short verb for not stopping something.
entries.definitionCN: 简短动词，指不加阻止。

entries.definition: It stresses handing something to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 强调把某物交给某人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The old verb meant to grant: to allow is to let something be given or done.
normal.cn: 古动词意为准许：allow 就是让某事被给予或被做。

normal.en: The same family also gives allowance and allowable.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 allowance 与 allowable。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase allow me.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「请让我来」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of allow in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 allow 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to let something happen, or to give time or money for a purpose.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「允许」时用它。

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：准许某人做某事。

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：让某事发生。

definition_zh: 小说；长篇小说；新奇的；新颖的；新颁律令（罕用）
definition_en: a long written story about imaginary people and events; also new and unlike anything seen before
core_image: 一本摊开的长篇手稿，纸页很新，故事却是从未有人讲过的
scene: 清晨的旧书店里，店主把一本厚厚的故事书摆到最显眼的位置。 She borrowed a novel from the library and read it in two nights.
sceneCN: 这里是「小说、长篇小说」（第 1 个义项：虚构的长篇故事）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本小说，两个晚上就读完了。场景里可辨的物件：旧书架、厚书、昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 novel 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小说家」
由 novel 加名词后缀 -ty 构成，义为「新奇；新鲜事」
由 novelist 加 -ic 构成，义为「小说式的；具有小说特点的」

senses.title: A long work of fiction
senses.definition: a long written story in which the events and characters are imagined rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 篇幅较长、情节与人物皆为虚构的书面故事
senses.example: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。
senses.why: The noun entered English from Italian novella, a short tale, and later grew to mean a full-length invented story.
senses.whyCN: 名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）进入英语，后来指篇幅完整的虚构故事；它和形容词「新」共用同一拉丁词根，因为故事讲的正是没见过的事。

senses.title: New and unlike what came before
senses.definition: new, original and not seen or done before
senses.definitionCN: 新的、独创的、此前未曾见过或做过的
senses.example: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。
senses.why: The adjective goes back to Latin novellus, a small form of novus meaning new, so freshness is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可追到拉丁语 novellus，它是 novus（新的）的小称形式，所以「新鲜」才是这个词最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: A newly issued decree
senses.definition: a new decree or supplementary constitution, especially in civil law
senses.definitionCN: 尤指民法中新增的法令或补充律令，现代英语已罕用
senses.example: The old code was amended by a series of novels.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法典经一系列新颁律令得到修订。
senses.why: In civil law the plural novels named the new constitutions added after the main code, keeping the bare sense of something newly issued.
senses.whyCN: 在民法传统里，复数形式 novels 指编入主法典之后的新律令，保留了「新颁之物」的字面意思；这个义项今天基本只出现在法律史里。

intro.en: Novel runs on two rails from the same Latin root: an adjective for what is new, and a noun for an invented story that was itself a novelty.
intro.cn: novel 沿着同一拉丁词根分出两条路：形容词指「新的」，名词指虚构故事，而这类故事在当时本身就是新鲜事物。

items.en: Novus meant new, fresh or recent, and it stands behind a large family of words about novelty.
items.cn: novus 意为新的、新鲜的、刚出现的，是表示「新」的一大族词的共同词根。

items.en: Novellus was a diminutive of novus, literally newish or young, and it passed into several Romance languages.
items.cn: novellus 是 novus 的小称，字面意思是「较新的、年轻的」，它进入了多种罗曼语。

items.en: Old French novel meant new or fresh, and English took the adjective with that plain sense.
items.cn: 古法语 novel 意为新的、新鲜的，英语借入的形容词就带着这层朴素的意思。

items.en: Italian novella named a short tale, and through French nouvelle it gave English the noun for a story.
items.cn: 意大利语 novella 指短篇故事，经法语 nouvelle 传给英语，成为表示「故事」的名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective novel for anything strikingly new and the noun novel for a full-length fictional work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词 novel 指「格外新的」，名词 novel 则指篇幅完整的虚构作品。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group collects words for stories and for newness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示故事与「新」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 篇幅较短的小说，或较长的短篇故事。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new thing.
entries.definitionCN: 新奇的性质，或新奇的小物件。

entries.definition: A person who writes novels.
entries.definitionCN: 写小说的人；小说家。

entries.definition: To introduce new ideas or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 引入新想法或新方法。

entries.definition: A person who is new to an activity or field.
entries.definitionCN: 刚接触某项活动或领域的新手。

entries.definition: Stories and characters that are invented rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的故事与人物，而非真人真事。

entries.definition: An account of events, whether real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的叙述，真实的或想象的。

entries.definition: New in design and not copied from anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 设计上新的，不是照搬别处的。

entries.definition: Recently made, arrived or thought of, and therefore new.
entries.definitionCN: 刚做出、刚到达或刚想到的，因而显得新。

normalIntro.en: The root nov means new, and from it grow the novel, the novelty and the person who writes novels.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 nov 表示「新」，小说、新奇与写小说的人都从它长出来。

normal.en: The Latin root nov means new, which is why a novel idea is simply a new idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 nov 表示「新」，所以 a novel idea 就是一个新想法。

normal.en: Novelty adds -ty to the same stem and turns new into a noun: the state of being new.
normal.cn: novelty 在同一词干后加 -ty，把「新」变成名词，指「新奇」这种状态。

normal.en: Novelist adds -ist, the suffix for a person, so it names the one who writes a novel.
normal.cn: novelist 加的是表示人的后缀 -ist，因此指写小说的人。

normal.en: Italian novella, a short tale, is the ancestor of the noun, which is why the two senses look unrelated.
normal.cn: 意大利语 novella 意为短篇故事，是名词义的祖先，所以两个义项看起来像是毫无关系。

normal.en: The adjective takes more novel and most novel, not noveler, because it is a longer adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词的比较级说 more novel、most novel，而不是 noveler，因为它属于较长的形容词。

abstract.en: A story and a new thing share one root because every story is, in a small way, something that did not exist before.
abstract.cn: 故事和新事物共用一个词根，因为每个故事在某种意义上都是过去不存在的东西。

abstract.en: Reading a novel means being handed a world that someone invented, so freshness lives inside the fictional sense too.
abstract.cn: 读一本小说，就是接过一个别人造出来的世界，所以「新」也活在虚构的那个义项里。

abstract.en: The word keeps two doors open: one leads to invention and one to novelty, and both open on the same Latin room.
abstract.cn: 这个词留着两扇门：一扇通向虚构，一扇通向新奇，而它们开在同一间拉丁语的屋子里。

examples.en: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。

examples.en: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
examples.cn: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。

examples.en: He writes novels about life in small mountain villages.
examples.cn: 他写关于山区小村生活的小说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹窝」——书里的故事闹成一窝，让人读到深夜；记住 novel 是小说。

root: 拉丁语 novus（新的）→ 小称 novellus（较新的）→ 形容词经古法语 novel 进入英语；名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）与法语 nouvelle 而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the Latin root for new; one branch names an invented long story, another describes anything strikingly fresh, and a third survives only in legal history.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是拉丁语表示「新」的词根；一条分支指虚构的长篇故事，一条形容格外新鲜的事物，第三条只留在法律史里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly written manuscript holding a story that nobody has told before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚写就的手稿，里面装着无人讲过的故事。

branches.en: a thick book left open on a night table
branches.cn: 床头摊开的一本厚书

branches.en: a reader refusing to close the last page
branches.cn: 读者舍不得合上最后一页

branches.en: a designer sketching a route no map has shown
branches.cn: 设计师画出一条地图上没有的路线

branches.en: a crowd hearing a proposal that breaks the old pattern
branches.cn: 众人听到一个打破旧套的方案

branches.en: a clerk copying a new decree into the law book
branches.cn: 书记员把新律令抄进法典

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin root for new, its adjective and its small form, plus two English suffixes that build the writer and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「新」的拉丁词根、它的形容词与小称之上，再由两个英语后缀造出「写的人」与「新的性质」。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus and its small form novellus supply the whole family, from the adjective novel to the noun novelty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 及其小称 novellus 支撑起整族词，从形容词 novel 到名词 novelty。

items.meaning: diminutive, marking something smaller or younger
items.meaningCN: 小称后缀：指较小的或较年轻的

items.meaning: person who does or makes something

items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：表状态或性质

definition_zh: 洞；孔；坑；漏洞
definition_en: an empty space or opening in something solid, or a gap where something is missing
core_image: 固体上被挖空的一块：能看穿它、能掉进去，也能藏东西
scene: 球场上有个小坑，足球正好滚了进去。 The ball rolled into a hole on the playground and stopped there.
sceneCN: 这里 hole 是「坑；洞」（第 1 个义项：实体上的空腔）；球滚进场上的小坑里停住了。

derivatives.zh: hole + -y → 有洞的；多孔的
与 hole 同族相关词 → 空心的；中空的
凹陷处；洼地

senses.title: An opening or cavity in something solid
senses.definition: an empty space or opening in something solid
senses.definitionCN: 实体物上的空腔或开口
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared into a hole in the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子钻进地上的洞不见了。
senses.why: The core sense is a space made where solid material should be.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「本该是实体的地方空了出来」。

senses.title: A gap where something is missing
senses.definition: a place where part of something important is missing
senses.definitionCN: 重要内容缺失的部分
senses.example: There is a hole in his story that nobody noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法里有个没人注意到的漏洞。
senses.why: A missing part of a story looks like a missing piece of a wall: an empty space in something solid.
senses.whyCN: 故事里缺了一块，就像墙上缺了一块：实体中留出了空位。

senses.title: An awkward or difficult situation
senses.definition: an unpleasant or difficult situation that is hard to get out of
senses.definitionCN: 难以摆脱的困难处境
senses.example: After losing the money, he felt he was in a deep hole.
senses.exampleCN: 丢了钱之后，他觉得自己陷入了一个深坑。
senses.why: Being stuck in a hole with steep sides makes a natural picture for a problem you cannot walk out of.
senses.whyCN: 待在四壁陡峭的坑里出不来，正好用来形容走不出的困境。

intro.en: Hole comes from Old English hol, an adjective meaning hollow, itself from the root of the verb helan, to hide.
intro.cn: hole 来自古英语 hol（中空的），其源头是动词 helan「藏、隐」的词根。

items.en: Old English hol meant hollow; the noun hole grew out of this adjective.
items.cn: 古英语 hol 意为「中空的」，名词 hole 由这个形容词演变而来。

items.en: The verb helan meant to hide or conceal; a hole is a space hidden inside solid matter.
items.cn: 古英语动词 helan 意为藏匿；洞正是藏在实体内部的空腔。

items.en: The family is Germanic; Dutch hol and German hohl show the same shape of meaning.
items.cn: 该词属日耳曼语族，荷兰语 hol、德语 hohl 意义相近。

items.en: In Middle English the noun was written hol or hole and named pits, burrows and openings.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 hol 或 hole，用来称呼坑、洞穴与开口。

items.en: Modern English widened the noun to gaps in stories, records and situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把该名词扩展到故事、记录与处境中的「空白、漏洞」。

note.en: Group one collects the sound-alike and same-root words; group two collects other names for openings.
note.cn: 第一组是同音与同根词；第二组是表示「开口、空腔」的近义词。

entries.definition: complete; all of something; it only sounds the same as hole
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；全部的；与 hole 同音但拼写与意义都不同

entries.definition: empty inside; having a hole or hollow space
entries.definitionCN: 中空的；与 hole 同族，指内部有空腔

entries.definition: full of holes
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，义为「有洞的；多孔的」

entries.definition: a large deep hole in the ground
entries.definitionCN: 地上又大又深的坑

entries.definition: a long passage dug through something
entries.definitionCN: 隧道；通道，强调可以通行

entries.definition: a space between two things or a missing part
entries.definitionCN: 缺口；缝隙，也指差距

normalIntro.en: Use sound pairs and real phrases to fix the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用同音对照与真实搭配记住 hole。

normal.en: hole and whole sound the same: the hole is empty, the whole is full
normal.cn: hole 与 whole 同音：hole 是空的洞，whole 是完整的全。

normal.en: dig a hole: the spade makes the empty space
normal.cn: dig a hole：铲子挖出的正是那块「空」。

normal.en: black hole: even light falls in and cannot get out
normal.cn: black hole：连光都掉进去出不来——洞的极端版。

normal.en: holey socks let the toes see the light
normal.cn: holey 的袜子让脚趾「见到光」——满是洞。

normal.en: A hole in a story is a missing piece, like a hole in a wall
normal.cn: 故事里的 hole 是缺了一块，像墙上缺了个洞。

abstract.en: Picture a solid wall, then a round empty circle where the wall used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一面结实的墙，再想象墙上凭空空出一个圆——那就是 hole。

abstract.en: Picture a rabbit disappearing: the ground opens and closes behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象兔子一钻，地面开合，转眼无踪——地洞的画面。

abstract.en: Feel a deep hole as a problem: steep sides, no ladder.
abstract.cn: 把深坑感受成困境：四壁陡峭，没有梯子。

examples.en: The workers dug a hole for the new tree.
examples.cn: 工人们为新树苗挖了一个坑。

examples.en: There is a small hole in my sock.
examples.cn: 我的袜子上有个小洞。

examples.en: Mouse holes appeared along the old wall.
examples.cn: 老墙沿线出现了几个鼠洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厚哦」——墙面很厚，却「哦」地空了一块，透出光来，这就是 hole（洞）。

root: hole 来自古英语 hol「中空的」，与古英语动词 helan「藏」相关，属日耳曼语族本族词；荷兰语 hol、德语 hohl 同源。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical opening the word extends to missing parts of stories and to hard situations.
sensesIntro.cn: hole 从实体上的开口，扩展到故事里的漏洞与难以脱身的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty space inside something solid
core.cn: 核心意象：实体内部的一块空

branches.en: a space you can see through or fall into
branches.cn: 能看穿或掉进去的空腔（义项 01）

branches.en: a missing part in words or records
branches.cn: 说法或记录里缺的一块（义项 02）

branches.en: a hard place with steep sides
branches.cn: 四壁陡峭、难以脱身的困境（义项 03）

branches.en: falling in is easy, getting out is not
branches.cn: 掉进去容易爬出来难（义项 01 · 03）

branches.en: a gap that lets light or error through
branches.cn: 让光或错误钻进来的缺口（义项 02）

intro.en: Hole is a short native noun with a tiny family, mostly adjectives.
intro.cn: hole 是短小的本族名词，词族不大，以形容词为主。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is its ancestor; Latin foramen is given for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁祖先；拉丁语 foramen（孔）列出作对照。

items.example: A hole appeared in the road.
The old adjective gave the noun its shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语形容词孕育了名词。

items.example: A hole hides inside solid matter.
His holey sweater lost a button too.
items.exampleCN: 他满是洞的毛衣还掉了一颗扣子。

items.example: The hollow tree hid the cat.
The whole class went to the museum.

items.meaning: a region where even light cannot escape
items.exampleCN: 黑洞能使空间本身弯曲。
拉丁 foramen 构成 foramen magnum。

definition_zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能；语言运用；（仪式的）进行；表演性
definition_en: the act of staging a work for an audience, the way a person, team, or machine carries out a task, the fulfilling of a duty, or the actual use of language as opposed to underlying knowledge
core_image: 舞台上的动作被观众看见并打分，或机器被推到极限，看它到底能跑多快
scene: 年终评审会上，经理把三条产品线的曲线投在墙上，逐条解释哪一条达标。 The manager put the performance curves of three product lines on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 performance 是「业绩」（第 2 个义项：个人或组织在工作上取得的成果与表现）；句意：经理把三条产品线的业绩曲线投在墙上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能

derivatives.zh: 表演；执行；履行；运转
表演者；执行者
施为性的；表演性的
表演性；施为性
表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A work staged for an audience
senses.definition: the staging of a play, concert, dance, or other work before an audience, taken as an event or an art
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前上演戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈或其他作品，作为事件或艺术看待
senses.example: The evening performance sold out two weeks in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 晚场演出提前两周售罄。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'to complete, to carry through'. A play is complete only when it is carried through in front of people: the script is the plan, performance is the doing.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为“完成、贯彻到底”。一部戏只有在人前贯彻到底才算完成：剧本是计划，performance 是做出来。

senses.title: How well a person or group does
senses.definition: the measured quality of a person's, team's, or organization's work against a standard or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或组织的工作相对于标准或预期的可衡量质量
senses.example: Her performance improved once the targets were made clear.
senses.exampleCN: 目标明确之后，她的表现有所提升。
senses.why: The same carrying-through is now watched by a manager rather than an audience. What matters is not whether the work is beautiful but whether it reaches the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同样是贯彻到底，只是这次看的是经理而不是观众。关键不再是作品美不美，而是它有没有达到标准。

senses.title: The carrying out of a task
senses.definition: the act of executing a task, duty, or function, often with attention to whether it was done at all and done correctly
senses.definitionCN: 执行任务、职责或功能的行为，常关注是否完成以及是否正确完成
senses.example: The performance of the repair took longer than the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项维修的执行比预估花了更长时间。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the plan is carried through. No audience and no score, only the difference between what was supposed to happen and what happened.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：计划被贯彻到底。没有观众也没有评分，只有“本该发生什么”与“实际发生了什么”之间的差别。

senses.title: What a machine can do
senses.definition: the speed, power, or efficiency with which a machine, vehicle, or system operates under test or load
senses.definitionCN: 机器、车辆或系统在测试或负载下运转的速度、功率或效率
senses.example: The engine's performance drops at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机在高海拔地区性能会下降。
senses.why: A machine has no will, but it can still be pushed to its limit. Performance becomes the measure of that limit, the carrying-through of metal instead of muscle.
senses.whyCN: 机器没有意志，但仍可被推到极限。performance 成了对这种极限的度量，是金属而非肌肉的贯彻到底。

senses.title: Actual use of language
senses.definition: in linguistics, the actual production and comprehension of speech in real situations, as opposed to the speaker's underlying competence
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指真实情境中话语的实际产生与理解，相对于说话者底层的语言能力
senses.example: Errors in performance do not prove a lack of competence.
senses.exampleCN: 语言运用中的错误并不能证明缺乏语言能力。
senses.why: Chomsky borrowed the word for the difference between knowing a grammar and using it under pressure. The plan inside the head is competence; the carrying-through in time is performance.
senses.whyCN: 乔姆斯基借这个词区分“懂语法”与“在压力下使用语法”。头脑里的计划是语言能力，时间中的贯彻到底是语言运用。

senses.title: One particular show
senses.definition: a single instance of presenting a work, countable and datable, as in the third performance of a run
senses.definitionCN: 呈现某作品的一次具体实例，可计数、可定时，如巡演中的第三场
senses.example: The Saturday performance was recorded for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 周六那场演出被录入了档案。
senses.why: A run of a play is many carryings-through. This sense counts them, which is why the word takes a plural and a date while the art sense does not.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏的连演是许多次贯彻到底。这个义项把它们数出来，所以这个词可以有复数和日期，而艺术义则不行。

senses.title: The carrying out of a ritual
senses.definition: the enactment of a ceremony, rite, or formal role according to prescribed words and actions
senses.definitionCN: 按规定的言语与动作进行仪式、典礼或正式角色
senses.example: The performance of the wedding rite lasted forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼仪式的进行持续了四十分钟。
senses.why: A rite exists only when it is done. Here performance is not entertainment but the condition of the thing existing at all, which shows how wide the 'carry through' sense is.
senses.whyCN: 仪式只有在被做出来时才存在。这里的 performance 不是娱乐，而是事物得以存在的条件，可见“贯彻到底”这一义项有多宽。

senses.title: The financial results of a business
senses.definition: the financial results of a company, fund, or economy over a period, measured in profit, growth, or return
senses.definitionCN: 公司、基金或经济在一段时间内的财务结果，以利润、增长或回报衡量
senses.example: The fund's performance trailed the index for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金连续三个季度的业绩落后于指数。
senses.why: Money is the scoreboard of the market. Performance here is the carrying-through of a strategy expressed as a number that can be compared with rivals.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是市场的记分牌。这里的 performance 是把战略贯彻到底后，用可与对手比较的数字表达出来的结果。

senses.title: Doing that makes what it says
senses.definition: the quality of an utterance or act that brings about what it describes, as when saying 'I promise' is itself the promise
senses.definitionCN: 话语或行为在说出或做出时同时实现其所描述之事的性质，例如说“我保证”本身就是保证
senses.example: The philosopher studied the performative side of promises and apologies.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家研究承诺与道歉的施为性一面。
senses.why: If a promise is completed by being spoken, then the saying is the doing. This sense pushes the 'carry through' idea to its limit: the performance is the only thing there is.
senses.whyCN: 如果承诺因被说出而完成，那么说就是做。这个义项把“贯彻到底”推到极限：表演本身就是唯一存在的东西。

intro.en: Performance comes from perform plus -ance (Latin -antia). Perform is not built on form: it comes from Anglo-French parformer, from Old French parfournir 'to accomplish, complete', literally per- 'thoroughly' + fournir 'to provide, furnish'. The original sense is 'to carry something through to the end'. English added the theatre sense in the 16th century, the machine sense in the 19th, and the linguistic sense in the 20th.
intro.cn: performance 来自 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 并不是由 form 构成的：它来自盎格鲁法语 parformer，再上溯古法语 parfournir“完成、贯彻”，字面是 per-“彻底”+ fournir“提供、供给”。本义是“把某事贯彻到底”。英语在 16 世纪加入戏剧义，19 世纪加入机器义，20 世纪加入语言学义。

items.en: Parfournir means 'to complete, to carry out fully'. The prefix par- is the French form of Latin per- 'thoroughly'; fournir 'to furnish, provide' is from the reconstructed Frankish form *frumjan.
items.cn: parfournir 意为“完成、彻底执行”。前缀 par- 是拉丁 per-“彻底”的法语形式；fournir“供给、提供”出自法兰克语的重构形式 *frumjan。

items.en: English perform first means 'to carry out, accomplish, execute' a task, promise, or duty. The spelling has no connection with form, despite the shared letters.
items.cn: 英语 perform 最早意为“执行、完成、履行”任务、承诺或职责。尽管拼写共享 form 几个字母，它与 form 毫无词源关系。

items.en: The theatre sense develops: to perform a play is to carry the script through into sound and action before an audience.
items.cn: 戏剧义在 16 世纪发展出来：演一部戏，就是把剧本贯彻成观众面前的声与动作。

items.en: Industry applies the word to machines and horses: performance is what an engine or animal can actually deliver under load.
items.cn: 19 世纪工业把这个词用于机器与马匹：performance 是发动机或牲畜在负载下实际能交付的东西。

items.en: Chomsky contrasts performance with competence in linguistics (1965), and management makes performance a measurable target.
items.cn: 20 世纪乔姆斯基在语言学中用 performance 与 competence 相对（1965），管理学则把 performance 变成可测量的指标。

items.en: Form, formal, and formative come from Latin forma 'shape'. Perform has no forma inside it: its fournir is 'provide'. The shared form- is spelling only, so performance is completion, not shaping.
items.cn: form、formal、formative 来自拉丁 forma“形状”。perform 里面没有 forma：它的 fournir 是“提供”。共享的 form- 只是拼写，所以 performance 是完成，不是塑形。

note.en: The first group separates perform's true family from the form trap. The second group compares execution, achievement, a show, and efficiency, the four words most often used in place of performance.
note.cn: 第一组把 perform 真正的词族与 form 陷阱分开。第二组比较执行、成就、演出与效率，这四个词最常被用来替代 performance。

entries.definition: to carry out an action, duty, or work before others. Performance is the noun of that carrying-through.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动、职责或在他人面前呈现作品。performance 是这一贯彻过程的名称。

entries.definition: a person who performs, especially on stage. It names the doer, while performance names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人。它命名做的人，而 performance 命名行为或其结果。

entries.definition: shape, structure, or a document with blanks. It comes from Latin forma 'shape' and has no connection with perform's fournir 'provide'.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、结构，或带空格的表格。它来自拉丁 forma“形状”，与 perform 的 fournir“提供”毫无关系。

entries.definition: shaping someone's development, as in formative years. It belongs to the forma family, so it is about shaping, not about completing a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塑造人成长的，如“形成期”。它属于 forma 词族，讲的是塑形，不是完成任务。

entries.definition: the act of putting a plan, order, or law into effect. It is close to performance in the task sense but carries no audience or score.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划、命令或法律付诸实施的行为。它在任务义上接近 performance，但不带观众或评分。

entries.definition: something accomplished, especially after effort. It names the result that stands, while performance can name the ongoing doing.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力而完成的事。它命名留下来的结果，而 performance 可以命名正在进行的做。

entries.definition: a public entertainment, or a display. It is the event sense of performance, but it can also mean an insincere display.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的娱乐演出，或展示。它对应 performance 的事件义，但也可以指不真诚的做样子。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful output to the resources used. It is one measured part of performance, not the whole judgement of it.
entries.definitionCN: 有用产出与所耗资源之比。它是 performance 中被测量的一部分，而不是对它的整体判断。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: Old French parfournir, fournir 'provide', the 16th-century stage sense, the 19th-century machine sense, and the form trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：古法语 parfournir、fournir“提供”、16 世纪的舞台义、19 世纪的机器义，以及 form 陷阱。

normal.en: Parfournir is 'to complete': a performance is a plan carried through to the end, whether on a stage, in a factory, or under a test load.
normal.cn: parfournir 是“完成”：performance 就是被贯彻到底的计划，无论是在舞台上、车间里，还是在测试负载下。

normal.en: Perform has no form inside it; its fournir means 'provide'. The resemblance to form is a spelling accident.
normal.cn: perform 里面没有 form；它的 fournir 意为“提供”。与 form 的相似只是拼写上的偶然。

normal.en: Theatre gave the word its audience, industry gave it a dial, and linguistics gave it a contrast with competence.
normal.cn: 戏剧给了它观众，工业给了它仪表盘，语言学给了它与“语言能力”的对照。

normal.en: The suffix chain is perform → performer → performance → performative, with -ance naming the act or result.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 perform → performer → performance → performative，其中 -ance 命名行为或结果。

normal.en: A performance review, a live performance, and an engine's performance are the same noun doing three jobs: judgement, event, and limit.
normal.cn: 绩效评估、现场演出与发动机性能，是同一个名词在做三件事：评判、事件与极限。

abstract.en: A score is only a plan for sound; the concert exists for one hour and then cannot be returned to.
abstract.cn: 乐谱只是声音的计划；音乐会存在一小时，然后就再也回不去了。

abstract.en: A machine has no ambition, yet we ask it to perform, as if the dial could be proud.
abstract.cn: 机器没有野心，我们却要求它“表现”，仿佛仪表盘会骄傲。

abstract.en: Saying 'I promise' does not describe the promise; it is the promise, made in the air between two people.
abstract.cn: 说“我保证”并不是在描述承诺；它就是承诺本身，在两个人口之间的空气里做成。

examples.en: The orchestra's performance was broadcast to a million listeners.
examples.cn: 乐团的演出被播给上百万听众。

examples.en: The company reported strong performance in the third quarter.
examples.cn: 公司报告第三季度业绩强劲。

examples.en: The contract requires the performance of the work by June.
examples.cn: 合同要求这项工程在六月前完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破佛曼斯」——演员“破”开剧本，把计划“佛”系地贯彻到底，站在台上做完 → performance 表演；表现；性能（只借音，不表词源）

root: 盎格鲁法语 parformer、古法语 parfournir「完成、贯彻到底」，由 per-「彻底」+ fournir「提供」构成；后缀 -ance（拉丁 -antia）构成名词。核心是「把计划贯彻到底，做到最后」。与 form（拉丁 forma「形状」）只是拼写相似，词根不同；四个主要义项分别是演出、表现、执行、性能。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of performance all describe a plan carried through to the end. What changes is who watches and what counts: an audience, a manager, a contract, a test bench, a grammar, a ritual, a market, or the very act of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: performance 的九个义项都描述一个被贯彻到底的计划。变化的是谁在看、什么算数：观众、经理、合同、试验台、语法、仪式、市场，还是说话这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plan driven through to the end while others watch and judge the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个计划在他人注视与评判下被贯彻到底。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE RITE: a work or ceremony carried through before witnesses, and one countable instance of it.
branches.cn: 舞台与仪式：在见证者面前完成的艺术作品或典礼，以及其中可计数的一次。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: a person's or firm's results measured against a standard, including financial results.
branches.cn: 记分牌：个人或公司相对标准的成果，包括财务结果。

branches.en: THE PLAIN DEED: a task or duty actually executed, with no audience beyond the contract.
branches.cn: 朴素的行为：实际执行的任务或职责，除合同外没有别的观众。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S LIMIT: what an engine or system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 机器的极限：发动机或系统在负载下能交付的东西。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AS DOING: actual speech use in contrast to competence, and utterances that accomplish what they say.
branches.cn: 作为行动的语言：与语言能力相对的实际言语运用，以及说出即做成的话语。

intro.en: Performance is perform plus -ance, from Latin -antia. Perform comes from Old French parfournir, not from form. The family is regular: -er the person, -ance the act or result, -ative the adjective, -ativity the abstract quality.
intro.cn: performance 是 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 来自古法语 parfournir，而不是 form。词族很规则：-er 人、-ance 行为或结果、-ative 形容词、-ativity 抽象性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is per- 'thoroughly' and the noun suffix -antia, which forms nouns of state or action. The verb itself is French, from Frankish *frumjan 'to provide'; Latin had no performare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 per-“彻底”与名词后缀 -antia（构成状态或动作名词）。动词本身是法语的，出自法兰克语 *frumjan“提供”；拉丁语并没有 performare 这个动词。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a task, or its public result
items.meaningCN: 任务的执行，或其公开的结果（-ance 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The performance of the pump was tested at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵的性能在低温下接受了测试。

items.meaning: to carry out, complete, or present
items.example: The team performed the test twice.
items.exampleCN: 团队把这项测试做了两次。

items.meaning: one who performs, especially on stage
items.meaningCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人（-er 施动者）
items.example: The performer left the stage in silence.
items.exampleCN: 表演者在沉默中离开舞台。

items.meaning: of an utterance that does what it says
items.meaningCN: 指说出即做成之话语的；施为性的（-ative 功能形容词）
items.example: A performative utterance changes the world by being said.
items.exampleCN: 施为性话语通过被说出而改变世界。

items.meaning: the capacity of acts or words to bring about what they name
items.meaningCN: 行为或言语产生其所命名之事的能力；表演性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: Gender performativity is a key concept in that field.
items.exampleCN: 性别表演性是该领域的一个核心概念。

items.meaningCN: 低于预期标准的表现（under- 低于）
items.example: Underperformance cost the division its bonus.
items.exampleCN: 表现不佳让该部门失去了奖金。

items.meaningCN: 比对手做得更好（out- 超过）

items.meaning: shape or structure; not related to perform
items.meaningCN: 形状或结构；与 perform 不同源
items.example: The form of the roof follows the wind.
They furnished the room before the guests arrived.
items.exampleCN: 客人到达前他们布置好了房间。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态或动作，构成抽象名词

senses.title: Train stop

senses.title: Broadcasting base

definition_zh: 合身；适合；安装；健康的；发作
definition_en: to be the right size or shape; to be suitable; healthy and strong; a sudden attack of illness or emotion
core_image: 把零件放进刚好形状吻合的凹槽里
scene: 试衣间里她拉上裤子的拉链，裤子不大不小正正好。 The new coat fits her perfectly.
sceneCN: 这里 fit 是「合身；大小合适」（第 1 个义项：尺寸或形状刚好吻合）；句意为新外套她穿正合身。

derivatives.zh: 由 fit 加动名词后缀构成，义为「试穿；装置；配件」

senses.title: To be the right size or shape
senses.definition: to be the correct size or shape for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或形状对某人某物刚好合适
senses.example: These shoes fit me well.
senses.exampleCN: 这双鞋我穿很合脚。
senses.why: Two shapes that match exactly are the picture behind every fit sense.
senses.whyCN: 两个形状恰好吻合，是 fit 一切义项背后的画面。

senses.title: To be suitable for a purpose
senses.definition: to be right or suitable for a purpose or job
senses.definitionCN: 对某个目的或工作来说是恰当的
senses.example: She is fit for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她胜任这份工作。
senses.why: What matches the slot in shape also matches it in function, so size became suitability.
senses.whyCN: 形状吻合的也恰能在功能上匹配，尺寸义于是引申为合适义。

senses.title: To put something into place
senses.definition: to put a part or device into the right place
senses.definitionCN: 把部件或装置安到正确的位置
senses.example: The workers fit new locks on the doors.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们给门装上新锁。
senses.why: Making a part match its slot means putting it in, so the matching motion became installation.
senses.whyCN: 让部件与槽位吻合就意味着把它放进去，匹配的动作于是变成安装。

senses.title: Healthy and strong
senses.definition: physically healthy and able to work or exercise hard
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康的、能胜任劳作或锻炼的
senses.example: He keeps fit by running every day.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天跑步保持健康。
senses.why: A body ready for hard work is a body made to the right shape, so suitability became physical health.
senses.whyCN: 随时能干重活的身体就是被塑造成合适形状的身体，合适义由此落到健康上。

senses.title: A sudden attack of illness or emotion
senses.definition: a sudden short period of illness or of strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或强烈情绪的突然短时爆发
senses.example: She had a fit of laughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她大笑了一阵。
senses.why: A seizure strikes suddenly like a part snapping into an unwanted place, so fit named sharp bursts.
senses.whyCN: 疾病发作像零件突然卡进不想要的位置，fit 于是被用来指急剧的爆发。

intro.en: Fit is an English word whose earliest sense was about matching and coming together.
intro.cn: fit 是一个英语本族词，最早的含义与吻合、凑合在一起有关。

items.en: Middle English had a verb fitten meaning to lead or adjust, and the noun fitte meaning a part of a poem.
items.cn: 中古英语有动词 fitten 意为引导、调整，名词 fitte 指诗歌的一个段落。

items.en: It is generally linked to a Germanic root meaning to tie or to join, the picture of parts coming together.
items.cn: 一般认为它出自日耳曼语词根，意为系、结，正是各部分合到一起的画面。

items.en: By the fifteenth century fitte also named a sudden outburst, from a fit of a song or laughter.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，fitte 也指突然的爆发，从歌曲或大笑的一阵引出。

items.en: Early Modern English fixed the senses of correct size, suitability and installation.
items.cn: 近代英语确立了尺寸合适、适用与安装等义项。

items.en: The health sense grew in the nineteenth century from exercise culture.
items.cn: 健康义项在十九世纪随锻炼文化兴起而生长。

note.en: Watch out for words next to fit that differ by one letter or one meaning.
note.cn: 留意与 fit 只差一个字母或一层含义的词。

normalIntro.en: Five quick ways to hold on to fit.
normalIntro.cn: 五个快速记住 fit 的方法。

normal.en: fit rhymes with bit and hit; all end in -it.
normal.cn: fit 与 bit、hit 押韵，都以 -it 结尾。

normal.en: keep fit is the most common phrase for staying healthy.
normal.cn: keep fit 是保持健康最常用的说法。

normal.en: fitting room is where you try on clothes.
normal.cn: fitting room 就是试衣间。

normal.en: a fit of laughter means a sudden burst of laughing.
normal.cn: a fit of laughter 指一阵大笑。

normal.en: outfit = out + fit, a full set of clothes to go out in.
normal.cn: outfit 由 out + fit 构成，指全套出门服装。

abstract.en: See the last puzzle piece press exactly into its gap.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一块拼图刚好按进缺口。

abstract.en: See a new shoe wrapping the foot, neither loose nor tight.
abstract.cn: 想象新鞋包裹住脚，不松不紧。

abstract.en: See a wrench closing on a nut at the exact size.
abstract.cn: 想象扳手恰好卡住尺寸刚好的螺帽。

examples.en: The dress fits her well.
examples.cn: 这条连衣裙她穿着正合身。

examples.en: He is very fit because he swims a lot.
examples.cn: 他身体很健康，因为他常游泳。

examples.en: They fitted a new window yesterday.
examples.cn: 他们昨天装了一扇新窗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「非特」——不是特别大也不是特别小，正合适

root: fit 是英语本族词，中古英语作 fitten、fitte，一般与日耳曼语中表示「系、结、使合在一起」的词根相联系。核心意象是两个形状吻合：尺寸吻合（合身）、功能吻合（适合）、位置吻合（安装），并引申出健康与发作等义。

sensesIntro.en: Fit grows from one picture of matching shapes: size, purpose, installation, health, and sudden bursts.
sensesIntro.cn: fit 从形状吻合这一幅画面生长：尺寸、用途、安装、健康，以及突然的爆发。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part snapping exactly into its slot
core.cn: 核心意象：零件恰好卡进凹槽

branches.en: Right size and shape
branches.cn: 尺寸与形状刚好

branches.en: Right for the purpose
branches.cn: 对用途合适

branches.en: Placed into position
branches.cn: 装到位

branches.en: Body ready for work
branches.cn: 身体能胜任劳作

branches.en: A burst that snaps in suddenly
branches.cn: 骤然卡进的爆发

intro.en: Fit works as a base for suffixes and compounds; the list shows how it combines.
intro.cn: fit 可作为后缀与复合词的基础，下面展示它的组合方式。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptus means fitted or suitable; it is a parallel word, not the ancestor of fit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aptus 意为贴合、合适，它是平行词，并非 fit 的祖先。

items.exampleCN: 厨房的固定装置是新的。

items.meaning: a person who does not belong
items.meaningCN: 不合群的人；不匹配之物
